title: Product Engineer
description:
Product Engineer

European Air-Cooled Chiller Engineering | Dublin, Ireland


What you will do


Johnson Controls has an exciting Product Engineer II opportunity based at our Dublin, Ireland location, supporting our new European air-cooled chiller engineering organization. If you enjoy mechanical design, testing, and data analysis, this could be the right position for you.

In this role you will support the mechanical design and performance of air-cooled chiller components and systems engineered for the European market, working under general supervision to complete detailed design work. You will provide support to production, laboratory, service, applications, and marketing teams across Europe, and contribute to new and exciting product development programs while continuing to build your expertise.


How you will do it

  • Develops and applies an understanding of the theories, concepts, technical principles, and processes related to the fluid, thermal, refrigeration, and other mechanical aspects of air-cooled chillers
  • Works under general supervision, following work instructions and defined processes to conceptualize and implement design ideas into the product
  • Defines and plans own activities for a project and completes detailed mechanical design work on assigned components and features
  • Applies European mechanical and safety codes and directives, including CE marking, the Pressure Equipment Directive (PED), and the Machinery Directive, and harmonized standards such as EN 378 (refrigerating systems safety) and EN 14511 (chiller performance rating)
  • Writes product specifications, and prepares, checks, and coordinates the release of documentation to support designs
  • Works with the design and manufacturing teams to develop layout concepts and system configurations that balance cost, performance, and reliability
  • Selects suitable mechanical components – including heat exchangers, fans, compressors, valves, and refrigerant piping – considering cost, performance, and reliability
  • Helps execute test programs to validate the performance and reliability of mechanical systems and components; analyzes, modifies, and troubleshoots mechanical sub-components based on test data
  • Responsible for engineering deliverables, including creating design specifications, detailed design reviews, data analysis, etc.
  • Supports the manufacturing and sustaining of the product, including initiating and executing design changes
  • Provides support to application engineers, designers, factory operations, product marketing, and product technical service, and can mentor new hires at the Engineer I level
  • Reports the status of own work, and that of junior team members, to the project team, with good written and verbal communication
  • Contributes to the accurate and on-time completion of projects and regularly reports on the status of assigned work
  • Continuously increases expertise across chiller design, theory, construction, operation, and applications; participates in process improvement
  • Uses standard technical and mathematical principles, theories, concepts, and best-practice methodologies in the field
  • Adheres to the Company’s Code of Conduct and Business Ethics standards


What we look for


Required

  • BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline / science
  • Minimum 2 years of work experience in a related field
  • Working knowledge of fluid and thermal principles
  • Working knowledge of European mechanical and refrigeration codes and standards (CE marking, PED, Machinery Directive, EN 378)
  • Proficient in mechanical design, able to conceptualize and implement design ideas into the product
  • Proficient with 3D CAD and the creation of production drawings to ISO / EN drafting conventions
  • Able to organize and process large amounts of data
  • Good written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, schedule-driven, team-oriented environment
  • Ability to travel up to 10%, primarily within Europe


Preferred

  • Experience engineering industrial products in engineer-to-order, applied, or made-to-order environments
  • Experience with product development and sustaining of configurable systems
  • Familiarity with refrigeration systems and the EU F-Gas Regulation
  • Familiarity with HVAC systems and motor-driven mechanical engineering design and test
  • Experience with structural, thermal, or computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis
  • Experience with ERP / material resource planning (MRP) software
  • Experience applying European regulatory standards such as EN 378, EN 14511, and the Ecodesign / ErP framework

title: Financial Accountant (Newly Qualified)
description:
Financial Accountant (Newly Qualified)

Finance | Dublin | Permanent


About Life Scientific

Life Scientific operates in a $250 billion global crop protection market.

We reverse-engineer off-patent products and deliver them with the same quality, safety and performance as the original - operating across multiple countries, currencies and regulatory environments.

As we scale internationally, complexity increases.

More entities.
More intercompany.
More inventory.
More moving parts.

Our Finance team is not a reporting function.

It is an enabling function.

And we are growing it deliberately.

The Opportunity

This role exists because we are expanding.

Not replacing. Building.

As a financial accountant, you will join a high-performing, commercially engaged finance team supporting a multi-entity, multi-currency business.

This is not a narrow ledger role.

You will gain exposure across:

  • Group reporting

  • Technical accounting

  • Audit

  • Tax compliance

  • Budgeting & forecasting

  • Cross-functional business partnering

You will work closely with senior leadership and operational teams - embedding financial clarity into a business that is moving quickly.

We are open to candidates from 1–5 years PQE.

What matters most is not just experience - but mindset.

This role is for you if you…

You enjoy structure - but don’t hide behind it.

You care about the integrity of the general ledger.

You instinctively question reconciling items that don’t feel right.

You can explain complex accounting clearly to non-finance colleagues.

You want to understand the business behind the numbers.

You’re comfortable operating in a multi-entity environment where intercompany and consolidation matter.

You don’t wait to be told what’s wrong - you go looking for it.

You are ambitious - and see this as a stepping stone into broader finance leadership.

You prefer building something in a scaling company over maintaining something static.

What You’ll Own

Financial Reporting & Ledger Integrity

  • Lead preparation of monthly and quarterly management reporting packs

  • Maintain general ledger integrity across multiple entities (accruals, deferrals, intercompany, reclasses)

  • Support group consolidation activities in a multi-currency environment

  • Ensure reporting is accurate, structured and delivered on time

Audit & Compliance

  • Own key elements of statutory audit preparation

  • Liaise directly with external auditors

  • Manage VAT, Intrastat and related compliance filings

  • Ensure adherence to IFRS / FRS 102 accounting standards

Commercial & Operational Support

  • Partner with Supply Chain, R&D and Commercial teams

  • Provide financial insight supporting operational decision-making

  • Contribute to budgeting and forecasting cycles

  • Support analysis that informs growth and investment decisions

Process & Scale

  • Contribute to automation and process improvement initiatives

  • Strengthen controls as the business grows

  • Support and mentor junior finance colleagues

What You Bring

You are a fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or equivalent).

You bring:

  • 1–5 years’ PQE

  • Strong grounding in technical accounting principles (IFRS / FRS 102)

  • Experience in multi-entity, multi-currency environments (group consolidation exposure is highly valuable)

  • Comfort operating in a deadline-driven, fast-paced setting

  • Clear communication skills - able to explain financial matters simply

Highly beneficial:

  • Audit training from a recognised practice

  • Exposure to manufacturing, stock or inventory environments

  • Experience working within ERP systems

But more important than background:

You are curious.
Structured.
Commercially aware.
And motivated to grow beyond traditional accounting boundaries.

What Success Looks Like

Within 18–36 months, you will have:

  • Strengthened ledger control and reporting clarity across entities

  • Built credibility with senior leadership and operational teams

  • Played a visible role in audit and compliance cycles

  • Contributed meaningfully to budgeting and forecasting

  • Positioned yourself for broader responsibility within Finance

Why Join Life Scientific?

Because this is not a static reporting role.

It is a growth role.

You will:

  • Gain exposure across technical, operational and commercial finance

  • Work in a flat, fast-moving structure

  • Have visibility with senior leadership

  • Help shape processes in a scaling international business

Life Scientific is building deliberately.

And this role is part of that build.

If you want early-career breadth, real responsibility and the chance to grow within a business that is scaling internationally - this is your platform.

title: Finance Graduate Pathways
description:
Job Description


The daa Finance Graduate Programme is a three-year programme designed for ambitious entry level graduates who want to build a career at the heart of a dynamic, global business. You'll gain exposure to the key finance functions that help power one of Ireland's most important transport hubs, while working in a fast-paced environment where innovation, automation, and digital transformation are shaping the future of finance.

Graduates will join the Early Careers Community, a network of interns, apprentices, and second-year graduates, offering opportunities to learn, collaborate, and build professional connections across the business.

You will join our Finance team from day one and remain with the wider finance team throughout your graduate journey. This allows you to develop deep technical expertise, build strong stakeholder relationships, take ownership of meaningful projects, and see the impact of your work over time.

As part of a global airport and travel retail group operating across 13 countries, you'll gain experience in a business that connects millions of people, supports international trade, and invests in sustainable growth. Working alongside experienced finance professionals, you'll gain exposure across areas such as Shared Services, Group Reporting, Forecasting, Budgeting, Tax, and Commercial Finance, contributing to projects that drive business performance and continuous improvement.

Alongside your role, you'll be supported in pursuing a professional accounting qualification giving you the skills, experience, and foundations to build a successful and future-focused career in finance.


Responsibilities


What will you work on:

As a Finance Graduate, you’ll embark on a dynamic three-year journey designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of our business and the finance function.

In Year 1, you'll build a strong foundation across key areas of the finance function, supported by a dedicated mentor who will help guide your development: Throughout the year, you will gain exposure to a range of key areas, including:

  • Forecasting & Budgeting: Support planning activities, including forecasting, budgeting, and capital investment processes.

In Years 2 and 3, you will deepen your expertise within a specialist finance team while continuing to broaden your understanding of the wider business. Supported by ongoing development opportunities, you will gain exposure to a range of key areas, including:

  • Tax: Assist with tax compliance, reporting, and planning activities.

Qualifications

Do you have what it takes?

We’re looking for curious minds and bold thinkers ready to shape the future of airport technology. To thrive in this programme, you should:

  • Exhibit learning agility, learning quickly, embracing feedback, and continuously developing new skills and capabilities.
  • Be strong collaborators, building effective relationships and working successfully across teams and stakeholders to achieve shared goals.
  • Align with daa's values and purpose, sharing our commitment to enabling business, connecting lives, and building a sustainable future.
What We Are Offering You ?
As a daa Finance Graduate, you will enjoy a comprehensive package of benefits designed to support your growth and reward your performance. As you work towards your finance qualification, you’ll benefit from a structured development journey that sets you up for long-term success.

Benefits include:

title: Junior / Graduate Safety Officer
description:
Role Summary

As part of our ongoing expansion, we are seeking a detail-oriented Junior / Graduate Safety Officer to join our team. Reporting to the Head of QHSE, ESG & Facilities, you will support the day-to-day management of health, safety and welfare across the company.

This is an excellent opportunity for a recent graduate or someone at the early stages of their career to gain practical experience within a busy manufacturing environment. You will work closely with colleagues across the business, developing your knowledge and experience while helping to promote a positive and safety-conscious culture throughout the organisation.

Company Profile

Capital Switchgear is a leading Low Voltage switchgear manufacturer, based in Rathcoole, Co Dublin. With over 50 years of expertise in switchgear design, manufacture, and installation, Capital prides itself on its high-quality, reliable products and a professional personal service tailored to each project. We are committed to supporting, developing, and empowering our employees throughout their journey with us.

Roles and Responsibilities

Health & Safety Duties:

  • Provide day-to-day support with the practical implementation of the company's health & safety policies and procedures.
  • Develop and maintain an awareness of the hazards associated with electrical switchgear products.
  • Maintain compliance with statutory health, safety and welfare requirements and also with relevant ISO standards.
  • Assist with hazard identification, risk assessments and the review of safe working practices.
  • Participate in regular workplace inspections and safety audits, recording findings and following up on agreed actions.
  • Assist with the preparation and maintenance of health and safety documentation, including Risk Assessments, Method Statements and related records.
  • Support the management of PPE, including monitoring availability, condition and appropriate use.
  • Assist with the reporting and investigation of accidents, incidents and near misses, ensuring appropriate records and follow-up actions are maintained.
  • Maintain accurate health and safety records, including inspection, training, incident and corrective action records.
  • Act as a Safety Representative and proactively contribute to Safety Committee meetings.
  • Assist with employee and contractor health and safety inductions and toolbox talks.
  • Support the delivery of health and safety awareness initiatives and campaigns across the teams.
  • Assist with monitoring statutory inspection, examination and testing requirements for equipment.
  • Support emergency preparedness activities, including emergency drills and testing of procedures.
  • Assist with health and safety visits to client sites where required.
  • Support with contractor management, including reviewing relevant documentation, delivering contractor inductions and monitoring performance.
  • Work with colleagues across all teams to identify opportunities to improve health and safety standards and working practices.
  • Follow up on assigned corrective and preventative actions arising from inspections, audits and incidents.
  • Act as a helpful and approachable point of contact for your colleagues in relation to day-to-day health and safety matters, escalating issues where appropriate.
  • Report unsafe conditions, damaged goods, equipment defects or other potential risks immediately.
  • Perform other duties related to health, safety and welfare as reasonably required by management.

Continuous Improvement and Industry Awareness

  • Contribute to the development and improvement of health and safety processes and systems.
  • Keep up to date with relevant health and safety legislation, guidance and good practice.
  • Maintain awareness of industry developments and applicable International (IEC), British (BS), European (EN) and other standards relevant to the business.

General:

  • Model Capital’s values and contribute to a collaborative, quality-focused environment.
  • Carry out your duties professionally and with integrity, maintaining confidentiality and discretion.
  • Take ownership of tasks and follow-up to resolve issues.
  • Be curious, adaptable, willing to learn and contribute to continual improvement.
  • Keep your work area clean, organised and safe, taking a "clean as you go" approach.
  • Follow environmental procedures, separating waste and using resources responsibly.
  • Complete all training and maintain the technical knowledge needed to do your role effectively.
  • Help out other teams as needed within the business.

Required Qualifications and Skills

Must Have

  • Diploma or Degree-level qualification in Health and Safety, Occupational Health & Safety or a related discipline, either completed or close to completion.
  • Solid knowledge of Irish Health and Safety legislation and workplace safety requirements.
  • Strong interest in developing a career in Health and Safety.
  • A practical and proactive approach to identifying and addressing safety issues.
  • Good organisational and administrative skills, with strong attention to detail.
  • Creative problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances.
  • Ability to work effectively with people at all levels of the organisation.
  • Good IT skills and confidence using Microsoft Office applications.
  • Committed, reliable and professional, with integrity and a willingness to learn.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • Committed, resilient professional who shows integrity and drive in everything they do.
  • Fluent in English and eligible to work in Ireland.

title: Ecologist- Barriers Mitigation Division
description:
Inland Fisheries Ireland (IFI) presents an exciting opportunity for a suitably qualified person to join a new team in IFI as an Ecologist. This role will primarily focus on providing ecological expertise to support the remediation works required to successfully mitigate or remove barriers to fish migration across Ireland.

The aim of the National Barrier Mitigation Programme is to improve river hydromorphology and connectivity in Irish catchments by strategically targeting significant barriers to fish passage and structures degrading river form, flow and function. Iconic species such as Atlantic salmon and the European eel are threatened species and IFI is mandated to protect them under law. Removing barriers will open up habitat to various species in an era where habitat loss is impacting severely on biodiversity both nationally and internationally.

The Ecologist will be responsible for ecological aspects of these projects, including preparing and reviewing Appropriate Assessment (AA) screenings, procuring ecological surveys and reports, undertaking ecological surveys, and ensuring alignment with the Habitats Directive and Wildlife Act. The Ecologist will be required to coordinate and undertake ecological surveys including fish habitat, mammal, invasive species, habitat, and electrofishing surveys as part of a team. The successful candidate will play a key role in guiding mitigation on projects from the initial feasibility and option selection phases through complex planning and consenting processes, all the way to project construction, environmental monitoring and completion.

The successful candidate will have demonstrated a high level of competence in relation to Appropriate Assessments under the Habitats Directive and will be required to both deliver and procure relevant reports. A comprehensive knowledge of ecosystem science and its associated statutory and regulatory processes will also be important. The work will involve the compilation of ecosystem and geographical data to support applications for consent for barrier removal or mitigation projects at river sites where river hydromorphology has been physically impacted by human activity. The successful candidate will also be required to contribute to the development of project plans, providing supporting documentation relating to Appropriate Assessment, WFD, fish populations and water quality/ecological status. The successful candidate will collate all necessary project details to secure necessary consents from relevant authorities.

Reporting to the Environmental Specialist, the Ecologist will be experienced in civil engineering works that pertain to the water based/marine environment and will have the ability to understand the impacts of ecosystem dynamics associated with barrier removal and mitigation.


ABOUT US

Inland Fisheries Ireland are the environmental agency responsible for protecting, managing and conserving Ireland's inland fisheries and sea angling resources.

More information can be found by visiting our website.

VISION, MISSION & VALUES

Vision

To place the inland fisheries resource in the best sustainable position possible for the benefit of future generations.

Mission

To protect, manage and conserve Ireland’s inland fisheries and sea angling resources and to maximise their sustainability and natural biodiversity.

Values

  • We are committed to the environment and sustainability.
  • We work collaboratively and with professionalism.
  • We communicate openly and transparently.
  • We act with respect, integrity, and accountability

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Main duties will include:

  • Day to day ecological input to projects under the supervision of the Environmental Specialist
  • Work closely with colleagues in the National Barrier Mitigation Programme to facilitate the implementation of barrier removal or mitigation projects, ensuring all ecological regulations and conditions are met.
  • Collecting, collating or sourcing ecological information such as survey data pertaining to mammals, bats, invasive species, habitats, fish, other aquatic species, and water quality data.
  • Co-ordinate and monitor the progress of Assessments through the IFI Appropriate Assessment Determination process.
  • Carry out ad-hoc Screening for Appropriate Assessment for development projects
  • Evaluate, prepare and present findings on ecological aspects of technical proposals, and make recommendations for incorporation into design and specifications.
  • Provision of essential information to IFI senior management and consenting authorities.

Management

  • Production of tendering and procurement documents for ecological surveys and assessments.
  • Coordinate habitat, electrofishing and other surveys for the wider environmental team.
  • Compilation of essential project details for submission to project stakeholders and partners including NPWS, consultants, contractors and relevant authorities.
  • Coordination or procurement of necessary environmental evaluations and assessments, ensuring that all required documentation is available and comply with regulatory standards.
  • Provide guidance and expert opinion on ecological receptors and associated regulations, to the wider NBMP team.
  • Compile standard operating procedures (SOPs) and risk assessments for the habitat restoration process.

Survey

  • Assist with fish stock, habitat and water quality surveys to support barrier mitigation projects.
  • Undertake surveys to identify invasive species, signs of mammals, bats, birds, habitats, aquatic species such as white-clawed crayfish and aquatic invertebrates.
  • Co

title: Associate Supervisors, Authorisation Associate and Data Analyst Positions
description:
The Central Bank of Ireland serves the public interest by maintaining monetary and financial stability while ensuring that the financial system operates in the best interests of consumers and the wider economy.

We currently have vacancies for Associate Supervisor, Authorisation Associate and Data Analyst positions on contracts of indefinite duration in the Banking and Payments, Capital Markets and Funds and Insurance Directorates. These roles are aligned with the Bank Executive grade. New entrants will commence on Point 1 of the relevant salary scale; in this case the starting salary will be €39,042. Please click here for further information on our salary scales.

These roles offer the successful candidates exciting career opportunities to work in a dynamic, collaborative and fast paced team that is responsible for the authorisation and ongoing supervision of a diverse range of regulated firms, in an increasingly complex and internationally focused environment. We are seeking to fill a range of roles across our banking, insurance and capital markets & funds supervision/authorisation teams.
Please be aware that as you are applying for a number of roles, your application will be assessed against each role, but you will only be interviewed once.

Responsibilities:

Bank Executives will undertake a range of tasks tailored to their specific division, which may include:
Supervisory Roles
  • Contribute to supervision of the sector across a range of key risks including Credit Risk, Solvency, Liquidity and Market Risks, Operational, IT, Consumer Protection and Integrity Risks to contribute to the safeguarding of the financial system. Analyse regulatory returns and other institutional information as appropriate to deliver robust and effective supervision, working in a collaborative way and sharing conclusions with colleagues.
  • Participate in institutional engagement meetings, offsite reviews, thematic / sectoral reviews, deep dives of specific risk and financial strategy topics to support the development of key supervisory recommendations.
  • Draw analysis-based conclusions and make recommendations to deliver robust, timely, effective and efficient supervision outcomes.
  • Provide briefings on key risk topics to drive strong firm engagements and clear supervisory actions.
  • Take responsibility for own work and ensure the outcome of supervisory work is communicated clearly and effectively to the team and management, and to the supervised firm where appropriate.
  • Maintain supervisory files, updating as appropriate for risk assessments and risk mitigation plans and contribute to the timely update of all records.
  • Develop and maintain positive stakeholder relationships in order to foster a culture of information sharing.
  • Carry out such other ad-hoc supervisory activities as determined by the Supervision Manager / Senior Supervisor, including administration so that the supervision team is fully supported in delivering their mandate.
  • Assess supervised entities compliance with relevant domestic and EU laws, regulations and policies.

Authorisation Support & Assessment (Authorisation Associate Role)
  • Contribute to the authorisation assessments of financial services firm applications using a risk-based, outcome-focused approach.
  • Undertake analysis of submissions and other available data to draw conclusions and make recommendations.
  • Participate in assigned tasks to assess issues, themes and risks that are identified in the authorisation process.
  • Monitor and maintain authorisation files from initial stages of the application, tracking assessment progress, ensuring timely updates and closure of files.
  • Contribute to and assist in the detailed assessment of governance, business models, policies/procedures, financial projections and capital plans (including ownership structures) submitted by applicants to ensure compliance with the relevant authorisation criteria and regulatory framework.
  • Carry out ad hoc assessment activities and provide briefings on key risk topics as part of supporting the authorisation process.
  • Internal and stakeholder engagement mainly through written communication to ensure clear delivery of team objectives.
Data Analyst Role
  • Contribute to desk based and themed reviews in relation to risk-based data analysis where appropriate and deliver output of same in accordance with the Central Bank’s risk assessment process, to contribute to the safeguarding of the financial system.
  • Contribute to the design, testing and implementation of a variety of internal IT system related changes in relation to areas such as regulatory returns and broader systems.
  • Contribute to the detailed analysis of the financial and regulatory return data for individual firms to ensure delivery of data-based supervision as appropriate. This includes contributing to the development of broader Supervisory MI and Analysis tools by working internally with colleagues in the Registry of Credits Unions and across the Central Bank.
  • Carry out such other ad-hoc divisional activities as may be determined by the Manager, such as participation in broader divisional projects. Be responsible for own work outcomes and communicate these effectively within the team, whilst also supporting the Manager in the development of other team members.
  • Provide relevant skills transfer and support to team members to share expertise and help to ensure skills, competencies and best practice are leveraged across the Division.

title: Systems Support Analyst
description:
Date: 1 Oct 2026

Location: Dublin, IE, D01 W213

Company: Walkers Global

We are a leading international law firm for global corporations, financial institutions, capital market participants and investment fund managers. With a global presence spanning the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, we advise on the laws of Bermuda, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Guernsey, Ireland and Jersey.

We treat everyone as the intelligent professional they are. Our approach is to trust and empower our people to deliver consistently, and enable them to succeed. Diversity is our secret weapon – it’s the sheer breadth of Walkers people that makes us who we are – gathered from across the globe and fluent in languages, jurisdictions and cultures that help us to mirror our clients and keep our own thinking in tune with the world in which we operate.


The Role


OFFICE: Dublin (Fully Onsite)


This is a support position that requires strong communication and customer service skills, as well as excellent technical knowledge. The Systems Support Analyst provides a customer interface for the IT Service Delivery team through the day-to-day operation and management of Walkers' IT Service Desk.


The Systems Support Analyst's principal duties are the support of Walkers' employees in the use of their computers and associated applications including Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, Aderant Expert, and iManage.


The successful candidate will provide support on the standard set of applications that are used by our lawyers, professionals and business services teams locally in Dublin and throughout our global offices, therefore the successful candidate must possess some level of expertise in Microsoft desktop operating systems, applications, and deployment and management systems. The successful candidate must also demonstrate the highest levels of customer service ability.


Duties & Responsibilities

  • Provide first-line support for hardware, software, and connectivity issues.
  • Manage and prioritize ServiceNow tickets, ensuring accurate logging, assignment, escalation, and SLA adherence.
  • Image, deploy, and maintain laptops, desktops, and mobile devices; assist with repairs and upgrades.
  • Install and configure Microsoft Office and other business-critical applications.
  • Support AV, video conferencing, VoIP telephony, and mobile devices, including meeting room setups.
  • Administer user accounts for onboarding, role changes, and offboarding.
  • Execute Joiners, Movers, Leavers (JML) tasks including account setup, hardware provisioning, and desk moves.
  • Monitor and manage IT inventory to maintain accurate stock records.
  • Communicate technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical users.
  • Collaborate with global IT teams to ensure consistent service delivery


Education, Skills & Experience

  • A bachelor's degree in an IT related discipline or equivalent and experience in a similar systems support role/IT Service Desk
  • Microsoft Windows operating systems (desktop and server), Microsoft Active Directory, and fundamental networking and communications technologies.
  • Microsoft Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, Azure Cloud, Group Policy, and SCCM.
  • ViewPoint, Aderant Expert and iManage.
  • Appreciation of ITIL or similar service management frameworks.

Working Arrangements

  • This is an onsite role requiring attendance from 9am to 5.30pm in our Dublin office on a 5-days per week basis
  • Participation in an on-call rotation that requires some weekend work on a scheduled basis (not more than 12 weekends per year) with appropriate time-off-in-lieu.
  • Ability and willingness to occasionally work outside normal working hours/days as required when requested.
  • Travel to regional offices as required.

title: Service Desk Support Analyst
description:
Location: Dublin 3
Job Type: Contract (12 Months)
Work Type: Onsite
Role Type: Service Desk Support

Overview of Role
We are looking for a Service Desk Support Analyst to join our internal IT team and provide high-quality technical support to end users across the business. The successful candidate will manage day-to-day incidents and service requests, troubleshoot hardware, software, access, and connectivity issues, and work closely with infrastructure teams on escalations. This role is suited to someone with strong customer service skills, good technical troubleshooting ability, and an interest in developing wider infrastructure knowledge, particularly across Cisco Networking, VMware, and Dell Technologies.

Role & Responsibilities:

  • Assist the Infrastructure and Network teams with any hands-on needs in either the Dublin 3 or Dublin 17 office.
  • Answer, evaluate, prioritise, and manage service desk tickets from internal users.
  • Provide first line and second-line support for hardware, software, operating systems, mobile devices, printers, and business applications.
  • Communicate with users by phone, email, instant messaging, and the service management platform, keeping them updated through to resolution.
  • Provision users, manage access requests, and support Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Exchange Online, groups, shared mailboxes, and distribution lists.
  • Troubleshoot end-user issues, perform root-cause investigations where appropriate, and escalate to infrastructure or application teams when required.
  • Assist with the installation, configuration, and ongoing support of IT hardware and software.
  • Monitor queues and incidents in line with agreed service levels and ensure tickets are fully documented.
  • Create and maintain knowledge base articles, support procedures, and troubleshooting documentation.
  • Support routine IT administration tasks and contribute to continuous improvement across the service desk.


Skills, Qualifications & Experience

  • Previous experience in a service desk, technical support, desktop support, or IT administration role.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to identify, investigate, and resolve technical issues.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft Windows environments and Microsoft 365 services.
  • Knowledge of Active Directory, DNS, user provisioning, permissions, and general IT administration.
  • Familiarity with Apple macOS support would be beneficial.
  • Knowledge of, or a willingness to learn, Cisco Networking, VMware, and Dell Technologies.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to support users at all levels of the organisation.
  • Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Professional, end user-focused approach with the ability to manage issues with sensitivity, tact, and ownership.


Experience:

  • ITIL Foundation knowledge or experience working within ITIL-aligned service management processes (desirable).
  • Exposure to Cisco switching, routing, wireless, or network troubleshooting (desirable).
  • Exposure to VMware environments, including virtual machines, vSphere, or related infrastructure concepts (desirable).
  • Exposure to Dell server hardware, iDRAC, firmware updates, or hardware diagnostics (desirable).
  • Meticulous and process-driven approach to support and documentation.


Education & Certifications:

  • Relevant third-level qualification in IT, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • ITIL Foundation certification (advantageous).


Role Details

  • Hybrid/home office working arrangements may be available depending on business needs.
  • The successful candidate must have access to a vehicle and hold a valid driving licence.
  • Travel may be required for up to 25% of the time.
  • This role offers the opportunity to develop broader infrastructure skills while supporting a busy internal service desk.


Visa:

  • Irish/EU Citizen or Stamp 4 Visa holder.

As Ireland's largest IT Solutions Provider with a growing global footprint, Ergo offers deep expertise across managed IT & hardware services, cloud, applications & software services, IT resourcing, and modern work solutions. description:

Overview

At Western Union, we’re more than a trusted name in global payments. We’re moving beyond remittances, beyond cash, and beyond the expectations of our customers.

Our talented teams enable us to transform into a digital-first company, built on the strength of our retail foundation and powered by next-generation payments. All this with the goal of helping people prosper.

Our customers inspire us to push boundaries and create services that make life easier and communities stronger. Wherever you are in the world, we’re committed to shaping the next generation of financial experiences.

Join us as we go beyond and be part of a team that’s redefining what’s possible.


Role Responsibilities

As an IT Risk Analyst within Western Union’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team, you’ll help strengthen how we identify, understand and manage technology, cyber and operational resilience risks. Working with colleagues across Technology, Information Security, Risk, Compliance and the wider business, you’ll gain exposure to a broad range of IT risk activities, including risk assessments, controls and regulatory requirements such as the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).   • Support the identification, assessment, monitoring and reporting of technology, cyber and operational resilience risks.

We are seeking candidates with experience in economics, engineering, legal, public policy and other relevant fields to fill posts in the following areas:

Security of Supply and Wholesale

Ensuring a secure energy transition to 2030, delivering on our 80% renewable electricity target and overseeing the wholesale all-island Single Electricity Market (SEM) in co-operation with the Utility Regulator in Belfast.

Networks and Economic Regulation

Working with Uisce Éireann and energy companies, enhancing the CRUs economic regulation of these critical networks, ensuring that they support customers, underpin economic growth and play a transformational role in climate change adaptation and mitigation.

Customer Policy and Protection (incl. Legal)

Empowering and protecting customers, overseeing competition and consumer protection across Irelands energy retail markets and playing an important role in supporting the National Energy Affordability Taskforce. Energy Safety

Regulating safety of gas (networks, supply, storage, use and liquefied petroleum gas distribution), petroleum (upstream onshore and offshore exploration and production of hydrocarbons), gas installers and electrical contractors.

Decarbonisation

Delivering new CRU regulatory frameworks for offshore renewables, green hydrogen, district heating and other new technologies and leading cross-cutting decarbonisation projects, including electricity connection policy, interconnector regulation and Projects of Common Interest.

Operations and Organisational Development

Supporting and empowering the CRU teams to achieve outcomes in our Strategic Plan in the areas of process improvement, finance and governance, human resources, information technology, and communications.

Reporting to a manager, the successful candidate will be involved in a varied role working to tight deadlines in a dynamic environment. CRU Analyst roles typically include activities such as:

About the Role – Placements The Online Graduate Programme includes two placements: Stretch Placement: A role outside your academic discipline that enables you to build new skills and broaden your understanding of the wider business Core Placement: A role aligned to your interests within the Online function, allowing you to develop specialist knowledge and expertise Each placement is structured around clear objectives and measurable outcomes, giving you the opportunity to make a tangible impact while accelerating your development. Throughout the programme, you'll gain exposure to a variety of online and digital disciplines, including: E-commerce and Online Trading Digital Customer Experience Online Operations and Fulfilment Website and App Performance Customer Journey Optimisation Digital Marketing and Customer Engagement Data Analytics and Reporting Online Innovation and Future Retail Technology You’ll work with cross-functional teams to analyse customer behaviour, identify opportunities for improvement, support digital initiatives, and help deliver a best-in-class online shopping experience. By the end of the programme, you'll have developed a strong understanding of how online retail operates, how digital experiences influence customer loyalty, and how data-driven decisions help drive growth within Tesco’s online business. Salary: €35,000 Programme start date: 6 September 2027 You will be responsible for
Alongside your day-to-day responsibilities, you’ll take part in a structured 18-month development programme that includes: Upskilling workshops focused on digital retail, e-commerce, data analytics, and customer experience Personal development sessions to build your confidence, communication, and leadership skills Store and fulfilment centre visits to understand how online orders are delivered from click to doorstep Networking opportunities with graduates and leaders across the business Mentoring and coaching from experienced colleagues who will support your career development At Tesco, graduates are given meaningful responsibility from the start, supported by a strong network of colleagues who are invested in helping you succeed. You will need
A genuine curiosity and desire to learn, develop and grow both personally and professionally. An interest in e-commerce, digital innovation and understanding customer behaviour. A positive and adaptable mindset, with the ability to embrace change and approach challenges as opportunities. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to share ideas and ask questions. A collaborative approach and a willingness to work effectively as part of a team. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an interest in using data to support decision-making. Enthusiasm, initiative and a proactive attitude towards learning and continuous improvement. A strong team spirit, supporting colleagues and contributing to a positive working environment. Whats in it for you?
Our Online Graduate Programme is designed for graduates who are passionate about digital innovation, e-commerce, and creating seamless online experiences for customers. If you're excited by technology, customer behaviour, and the ever-evolving world of online retail, this programme will give you the opportunity to develop your skills in one of the fastest-growing areas of Tesco Ireland. From day one, you'll be part of a dynamic team that helps deliver Tesco’s online shopping experience, ensuring our customers can shop wherever and whenever they choose. You’ll work on real projects that support the growth of our online business, from improving digital journeys and customer experience to driving online sales and operational efficiency. Annual Leave: Starting at 23 days per annum About Us
Our core purpose, "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day" means we always keep customers at the heart of what we do, while also reflecting our responsibilities to the communities we serve and to society more broadly. At Tesco, inclusion means that Everyone’s Welcome. Everyone is treated fairly and with respect; by valuing individuality and uniqueness we create a sense of belonging. Diversity and inclusion have always been at the heart of Tesco. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best. Across the Tesco group we are building an inclusive workplace, a place to actively celebrate the cultures, personalities and preferences of our colleagues – who in turn help to build the success of our business and reflect the diversity of the communities we serve. Our office is based in Dun Laoghaire, Co. Dublin and Tesco has embraced hybrid working. We have open plan offices and informal breakout spaces so teams can collaborate together. We’ve a subsidised colleague restaurant for all breakfast, lunch and snack requirements. At the weekly “Team 5” update you'll get to hear about exciting events happening across our stores and any important business updates. We have stunning views of Dublin Bay from our office and are ideally located next to public transport options and lots of handy amenities in the local area.

description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title and Summary

Site Reliability Engineer II

RiskPS BizOps team is looking for a Site Reliability Engineer who can help us solve problems, implement automation, and leverage best practices.
  • Are you a born problem solver who loves to figure out how something works?
  • Are you a detail -oriented individual who enjoys complex problem solving?

Experience in working across development, operations, and product teams to prioritize needs and to build relationships is a must.

Mission
The role of business operations is to be the production readiness steward for the platform. This is accomplished by closely partnering with developers to design, build, implement, and support technology services. A business operations engineer will ensure operational criteria like system availability, capacity, performance, monitoring, self-healing, and deployment automation are implemented throughout the delivery process. Business Operations plays a key role in leading the Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) transformation at Mastercard through our tooling and by being an advocate for change and standards throughout the development, quality, release, and product organizations.

We accomplish this transformation through supporting daily operations with a hyper focus on triage and then root cause by understanding the business impact of our products. The goal of every biz ops team is to shift left to be more proactive and upfront in the development process, and to proactively manage production and change activities to maximize customer experience and increase the overall value of supported applications. Biz Ops teams also focus on risk management by tying all our activities together with an overarching responsibility for compliance and risk mitigation across all our environments. A biz ops focus is also on streamlining and standardizing traditional application specific support activities and centralizing points of interaction for both internal and external partners by communicating effectively with all key stakeholders.

Ultimately, the role of biz ops is to align Product and Customer Focused priorities with Operational needs. We regularly review our run state not only from an internal perspective, but also understanding and providing the feedback loop to our development partners on how we can improve the customer experience of our applications.

title: Controls Engineer
description:
Work Your Magic with us! Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That`s why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.


The Role

The Automation and Controls Specialist is responsible for designing, programming, and implementing control strategies to optimize manufacturing processes using advanced automation technologies. This role requires proficiency in configuring and troubleshooting systems such as PLCs, SCADA, DCS, and HMI.
While the role focuses on Smart Manufacturing and CapEx projects implementation, on a day-to-day it may also support diagnosis and resolution of issues related to control systems.

Duties

  • Design, develop, install, modify and test the programming of PLC's, Robotics, vision systems as well as supporting the sites SCADA systems.
  • Responsible for repairing, fault finding, and troubleshooting automation issues on production equipment as part of a team working in a live production environment.
  • Collaborate with team members to implement effective repairs and improvements.
  • Develop knowledge of on-site systems and equipment such as PLC's, Servo motors, vision systems and robotics to become the Site SME for these technologies. Lead or manage the development of GAMP documentation with the project team e.g. URS, FDS, FAT, SAT etc...
  • Participate and in some cases lead projects, provide technical support and make informed decisions on hardware and architecture selection.
  • Monitor and analyze opportunities for the development of new or improved tools for process improvement activities. Define the equipment and technologies to be used in the department based on experience in the area.
  • Support the site during out of hours with automation issues as part of the Automation Oncall service as part of the Automation On-call team rota.
  • Have a keen ability to fault find complex automation equipment including interrogation ofprogram code to identify issues.
  • Coach area technicians and junior control engineers as required and support problemsolving and continuous improvement efforts across all areas of Biotools.
  • Carry out justification for capital projects for the site and lead all elements of the projectwithin schedule and costs
  • Manage all Requisitions and financial needs to ensure site discretionary budgets and capitalbudgets are met.
  • Give input to the budgeting process for controls automation needs to allow the correctfinance to be put in place for execution.
  • Ensure project design and installations meet the requirement of EU directives such as the Machinery Directive and CE compliance.
  • Ensure Electrical Control Panels are built to standard and adhere to Safety of Machinery –EN60204-1.
  • Develop critical spares list for site controls and automation hardware & ensure that criticalspares are in stock or are readily available at all times. Ensure that an effective program is then maintained.
  • Investigate EHS incidents, lead RCAs and complete EHS actions as appropriate.
  • Perform all tasks with due recognition of safety, environment, GMP & plant procedures.

Who You Are

  • BEng degree in electrical/electronic/automation engineering or equivalent, with particularemphasis in the automation discipline.
  • Minimum of 7 years + industry experience in an FDA or GMP environment as an automation controls engineer. Electrician experience and qualification is desirable.
  • Experience with Robotic/pick &place Machines with high speed assembly operations required.
  • Knowledge of interfacing with and controlling of servo drive and Motion Control systems.
  • Knowledge of Vision Systems is preferable. [Cognex and other Vendors]
  • Experienced with Rockwell, Siemens S7, Telemecanique and other types of PLC Controllers.
  • In depth knowledge of automation network protocols including EtherNet IP, DeviceNet,ControlNet, Modbus and Profibus.
  • Knowledge of control systems integration with plant MES (Manufacturing Execution System).
  • Excellent problem solving and analytical ability and the ability to work as part of a team.
  • Be familiar with planned preventative maintenance approaches.
  • Excellent awareness and experience in relation to Quality and Health, Environment andSafety.
  • Management of projects through their full life-cycle.
  • Knowledge of CE marking and declaration of conformity reviews and approvals.
  • A knowledge of IT systems that support manufacturing equipment.
  • Lead Machine Improvement Initiatives to increase reliability or productivity.
  • Electrical and machine control system problem solving
  • Familiar with GMP requirements within a regulated industry.
  • Excellent verbal, written & interpersonal communication skills.
  • Motivated team player with pro-active and flexible approach to work.
  • Ability to deliver on time and meet tight deadlines.

  • Capable of working on several projects with different businesses, priorities and designrequirements.

title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Networking
description:
DESCRIPTION

Are you a developer passionate about building incredible software? Committed to quality, agility, and consistency? Curious how software and AI/ML can operate and maintain one of the world's largest networks?

If so, come join us — automate the future of global networks at unprecedented scale, and thrive in a team where your voice matters.

AWS Infrastructure Services is looking for a Software Development Engineer to join the Data Center Network organization. We're the people who keep the cloud running — owning the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In this role, you'll work with customers, leadership, and peers to automate and invent new ways of operating the AWS network. You'll build best practices, improve operational procedures, and deliver iterative impact with a proactive mindset. You'll collaborate across AWS to deliver the highest standards of safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost. You'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. You'll be responsible for building software services that deploy and scale the Amazon networks supporting AWS, customers, and other business units across multiple global datacenters.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
  • Shape the automation future in networking
  • Build and maintain production-quality distributed systems at startup pace
  • Develop tools and processes that collect and rationalize data from multiple sources to reduce workloads
  • Use data to measure success; take ownership of service quality and proactively prevent customer-facing faults
  • Partner with Network Engineering teams for fast, smooth software roll-outs
  • Identify and troubleshoot recurring platform issues; escalate effectively to senior engineering teams
  • Design and build cloud-computing system software for a diverse set of customers
Mentor junior engineers and bring clarity to ambiguous situations
  • Identify and implement optimizations for performance, scalability, and efficiency

A day in the life
You will work with customers to gather requirements and generate technical designs, and you will carry the project through all the software lifecycle stages. You’ll develop products that enable builders to develop and operate robust, high-quality software and safely, securely, and reliably deploy it. You will use your technical expertise and communication skills to mentor other engineers and provide training and support for our technologies. You will have access to leadership and engineering staff.

About the team
The AWS DCFC (DCF Controllers) team owns the software controller within the CLOS Fabric Engineering (CFE) organization. The team is responsible for building software that monitors the network/fabric state, recovers out-of-service capacity, enables network scaling, manages IP allocation, and plans and executes decommissioning.
The broader CFE organization focuses on designing cost-effective CLOS topologies, maximizing port availability, and managing the full platform lifecycle—from hardware qualification through decommissioning.   • Undertake site visits and site surveys, meeting with Clients and Stakeholders and collaborating with others, both within Arup and external to Arup

Is this role right for you?

An undergraduate or bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in the following disciplines:

  • Maritime Engineering
  • Civil Engineering
  • Environmental Engineering
  • Coastal Engineering
  • Geotechnical Engineering
  • Naval Architecture
  • Structural Engineering
  • Ground / Geotechnical Engineering
  • Materials Science
  • Floating Structures

Desired skills and attributes

  • A basic understanding of maritime, coastal and civil engineering principles.
  • An interest in coastal processes, geotechnics, structures and environmental considerations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • A curious mindset and willingness to learn.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • A passion for sustainable and resilient infrastructure solutions.

To be considered for a graduate opportunity, your application must include a copy of your academic transcript and meet the following criteria:

  • No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role

title: Software Engineer III
description:
Job Description:

Here at Rakuten Kobo Inc. we offer a casual working start-up environment and a group of friendly and talented individuals. Our employees rank us highly in terms of commitment to work/life balance. We realize that for our people to be innovative, creative and passionate they need to feel valued and supported. We believe in rewarding all our employees with competitive salaries, performance based annual bonuses, stock options and training opportunities.


If you’re looking for a company that inspires passion, personal, and professional growth – join Kobo and come help us on our mission of making reading lives better.


The Role:

Rakuten Kobo Ireland is looking for a Software Engineer III to join our amazing Web team! This is a remote position based in Dublin, Ireland.

You will be joining one of our development strike teams to deliver awesome new features for our many users to enjoy.

Our engineers are enthusiastic and operate across the development spectrum, from front-end to back-end to CI/CD and infrastructure. We take full responsibility for our work, from requirements gathering and solutioning, to implementation and testing, to deploying and monitoring how our code behaves in front of real customers. Kobo is looking for an engineer who shares these passions and is proud of the work they do.

Reporting to the Software Engineering Manager, the Full Stack Software Engineer III plays a vital role in all aspects of delivery from design, planning and implementation through to releasing and monitoring.


Responsibilities:

  • Building quality software using the full Microsoft stack including MVC Web Applications, Web API services, .Net 8 microservices and much more.
  • Propose designs and Proof of Concepts to Architecture team and work with the team to deliver the implementation to Production.
  • Participate in code reviews; happy to give and receive constructive feedback.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively with teammates, Business stakeholders and other development teams in Kobo.
  • Mentoring more junior team members of the team and conducting code reviews.


The Skillset:

Required

  • Computer Science or Computer Engineering Degree (or equivalent experience)
  • Highly technical and able to communicate well with engineers and cross-functional team members
  • Experience with C#, ASP.NET MVC, WebAPI, RESTful Services, .Net 8 Microservices
  • Experience with SOLID Principles and Practices, IoC & TDD.
  • Some experience with service bus technology e.g. NServiceBus, RabbitMQ.
  • Strong experience with React and modern JavaScript/CSS frameworks.
  • Experience with Git.
  • Experience with designing, implementing, and optimizing observability solutions (metrics, logs, traces).
  • Experienced and knowledgeable in CI/CD and different testing strategies and techniques (Unit, Integration, UI tests), including experience with ArgoCD.
  • Comfortable with and enthusiastic about learning new technologies.


Nice to Haves

  • Working in an Agile environment and teamDocker, Solr, Kubernetes
  • Test automation using Selenium Webdriver or Playwright
  • Working with GitHub or Azure DevOps
  • Knowledge of Ruby or other scripting languages
    • Experience with MS SQL, RavenDb, EntityFramework.

The Perks

  • Flexible hours and remote working environment
  • 4 extra long weekends around bank holiday weekends
  • Full benefits starting from your first day
  • Paid volunteer days, unlimited sick days
  • 4% employer pension contribution
  • Flexible spending account
  • Talent and development training budget
  • Free Kobo device + free weekly eBook or audiobook
  • Weekly Kobo Spark sessions
  • Maternity/paternity leave top-up


About Rakuten Kobo Inc.
Rakuten Kobo Inc. is the world’s digital bookseller created by and for booklovers. Owned by Tokyo-based Rakuten Group, Inc. and headquartered in Toronto, Rakuten Kobo’s millions of worldwide users can read anytime, anywhere, and on any device. With a mission to make reading lives better for all, Rakuten Kobo connects readers to stories using thoughtful and personalized curation of eBooks and audiobooks, and the best dedicated eReaders and apps for reading. With the singular focus of making reading lives the best they can be, Kobo’s open platform allows people to fit reading into more moments in their busy lives. To learn more about Rakuten Kobo, visit www.kobo.com.


Rakuten Kobo Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. Accessibility accommodations for candidates with disabilities participating in the selection process are available on request. Any information received related to accommodation needs of applicants will be addressed confidentially.


Rakuten Kobo would like to thank all applicants for their interest in this role however only qualified candidates will be shortlisted.

title: Systems Engineer, European Sovereign Cloud
description:
DESCRIPTION

AWS has successfully launched the European Sovereign Cloud (ESC), marking a significant development in Utility Computing (UC). To spearhead this initiative, we are actively seeking experienced systems engineers with a strong background in automation and operations. As part of the AWS Managed Operations team, you will play a pivotal role in building, operating and evolving operations and development teams dedicated to delivering high-availability AWS services, including EC2, S3, Dynamo, Lambda, and Bedrock, exclusively for EU customers. For more information on ESC please check out our blog: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/in-the-works-aws-european-sovereign-cloud/

Your responsibilities will encompass overseeing the ongoing operations and expansion of the ESC, working closely with global AWS teams, and influencing the evolution of AWS services and technology. A typical day in this role involves collaborating with technology leaders, contributing to the enhancement of day-to-day operations, and ensuring continuous improvements in availability, reliability, latency, performance, and efficiency of the ESC. You will be required to occasionally participate in “on-call” rotations to resolve incidents occurring out-of-hours.

The overarching goal is to deliver scalable services and ensure a high-availability experience for EU customers. If you are an experienced professional ready for a challenging and impactful opportunity, we invite you to join our efforts in operating and scaling a best-in-class development engineering and operations team that aligns with AWS' commitment to customer satisfaction and continual innovation.

A day in the life
Embark on a week filled with meaningful contributions to the operation and improvement of significant software systems. You dedicate a substantial portion of your time to carefully review the operational health of services within your team's responsibility. In the process, you diligently identify anomalies and craft actionable bug reports, aspiring to enhance the overall efficiency and performance of your systems.

In addition to these responsibilities, you offer constructive feedback on change management documents and work earnestly to address your team's operational backlog. Through a collaborative effort, you strive to navigate challenges and ensure the seamless functionality of your systems. Additionally, you engage in the development and testing of scripts, hoping to provide practical solutions to enhance your workflows.

Beyond the technical aspects, you assume a role as an educator, sharing insights on the complexities of the European Sovereign Cloud with service teams. It's a humbling experience for you to contribute to the collective knowledge of the team, fostering a culture of mutual understanding.

This week encapsulates your commitment to continuous learning and improvement, acknowledging that every effort, no matter how small, contributes to the collective success of your team and the reliability of your software systems.

In addition to these responsibilities, your position involves 24x7 on-call responsibility. You work as a team to root-cause issues and ensure your systems remain resilient and fault-tolerant, underscoring your commitment to maintaining operational excellence.

Eligibility requirement
  • Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
  • Candidate must be a national of an EU member state and residing in the EU to operate the AWS European Sovereign Cloud.
  • Amazon will provide relocation support for successful applicants relocating within the European Union.
  • Employees will participate in an On-Call rota.

About the team
Utility Computing (UC)
European Sovereign Cloud (ESC) is a part of AWS Utility Computing (UC).

title: Graduate Utilities Engineer
description:
Main Purpose and Objectives of Position

The Graduate Utilities Engineer is an entry-level engineering role, designed to build the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to support the reliable operation and qualified state of clean utility systems and supporting grey systems within Biotech manufacturing. Working closely with mentors and experienced engineers, the Graduate Utilities Engineer will progressively develop the technical and professional capability to help ensure processes are in-control and compliant, while contributing to process continuous improvement as part of a structured development programme.

The following are the main areas of development for the Graduate Utilities Engineer role:

● Develop a strong safety mindset by following safety rules and actively contributing to improving the safety culture.

● Build clean system engineering knowledge as a developing member of the area team, supported by experienced colleagues.

● Learn how clean system unit operations and equipment are maintained in a qualified and reliable state.

● Gain exposure to establishing and monitoring critical parameters for clean systems, to support processes remaining in control.

● Support troubleshooting of unit operations, equipment and operational issues, building problem-solving skills under guidance.

● Learn to evaluate activities for their impact on the qualified state of equipment, and to use the appropriate tools and processes.

Personal Considerations: At times, the Graduate Utilities Engineer may need to travel offsite to other locations, other companies, conferences, off-site training, or to support capital projects.

Educational Requirements: Third Level Engineering Qualification (recent graduate, or in final year of study)

License/Certificate Requirements: None

Language Requirements: Proficient in English

Key Responsibilities

In line with the job outlined above, and as part of a graduate development plan, the following are typically the key tasks the role will be introduced to and will grow into over time, with support from a mentor and the wider team:

Safety

● Learn to contribute to the safe design and safe operation of equipment within the area.

● Actively participate in safety-related activities (audits, hazard reviews, pre-start-up safety reviews) to build safety awareness and drive ongoing improvement.

Bio-process Technical Support

● Develop into a competent point of contact for equipment and processes in an assigned area of responsibility, building a clear understanding of unit operations and associated equipment.

● Learn to monitor clean utility systems and support the optimisation of unit operations and equipment performance.

● Support troubleshooting efforts relating to unit operations, equipment and operational issues, working alongside experienced engineers.

● Learn and apply formal problem-solving techniques, including Root Cause Analysis, to help resolve unit operations and equipment issues.

● Respond to unit operations issues and equipment failures under guidance, document appropriately, and support resolution of events through appropriate actions.

● Communicate effectively with others, especially team members, operations and crafts personnel.

Maintain Qualified and Reliable State

● Learn to evaluate activities for their impact on the qualified state of unit operations/equipment, and to use the appropriate business processes (e.g. change control).

● Gain exposure to system/component classification and maintenance strategy for equipment.

● Support the implementation of corrections, corrective actions, and countermeasures arising from investigations.

● Participate in Periodic Reviews for systems and equipment.

● Support IQ/OQ/PQ activities (including commissioning activities of new unit operations/equipment), building towards leading elements of this work with experience.

Asset Management

● Contribute to the scoping of capital projects targeted at both short and longer-term needs, and support the user representative role for local projects.

● Build an understanding of equipment reliability issues, with the objective of identifying improvement opportunities.

Improve the Business

● Identify and support improvement opportunities (procedural changes, upgrades, projects etc.) associated with unit operations/equipment within the area.

Job Types: Full-time, Permanent

Work Location: In person

description:

Engineering & Quantity Surveying Graduate Development Programme 2027

Are you ready to apply your engineering or quantity surveying skills to one of the most ambitious and impactful infrastructure transformations in Ireland?

Do you have, or are you about to get, a degree in Electrical/Telecoms, Civil/ Structural, Mechanical / Energy Engineering or as a Quantity Surveyor?

If so, the ESB Technical Graduate Programme is your opportunity to work at the forefront of Ireland’s clean energy transition, designing, building, and maintaining the electricity network that connects homes, businesses, and communities across the country.

With over 1000 engineers, quantity surveyors and related technical professionals, ESB is dedicated to investing in engineering related expertise and developing critical skills to support Ireland’s future growth and development.

ESB’s Technical Graduate Programme is designed for STEM graduates with less than two years’ experience, offering structured development, real responsibility, and the opportunity to contribute to our Net Zero by 2040 strategy. At ESB, we believe our people are the driving force behind everything we do - today and into the future. That’s why investing in your growth, development and potential isn’t just part of our strategy, it’s at the very heart of it.


The programme has a wide variety of opportunities:


You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, quantity surveyors and technical professionals on projects that matter.


What You’ll Work On:


  • Delivering energy infrastructure projects for Ireland, with opportunities to be involved at every stage of the project lifecycle
  • Designing, planning and building the electricity network of the future
  • Helping to shape ESB's generation fleet on site, ensuring the safety, reliability and resilience of our thermal and renewable energy facilities
  • Supporting Ireland's largest private telecoms network, helping keep ESB's infrastructure connected and operating safely
  • Supporting ESB’s customers to optimise their energy use & develop sustainable energy solutions

Our bespoke Early Career Technical Talent Programme includes:


  • Structured, timely learning and development through formal as well as on-the-job opportunities
  • Work assignments giving appropriate breath of learning to facilitate career progression
  • Performance targets set to challenge & develop you while you contribute to ESB’s strategy
  • Mentoring & career support to enable you to find the right career in the company
  • Social networking to develop peer supports & relationships across ESB

In addition:


As an employee on our Technical Graduate Programme, you will enjoy our many benefits including a competitive salary and bonus, performance related promotions and a comprehensive benefits package built on the four pillars of reward, career, community, and wellbeing.


Location


Nationwide


What We Look For:


  • A Masters, Honours or Ordinary degree (or near completion in 2027) in Electrical/Telecoms, Civil/Structural, Mechanical/Energy Engineering or Quantity Surveying, with a minimum Second Class Honours Grade 1 (2.1) result
  • Excellent analytical skills combined with the ability to learn quickly
  • Proven ability to deliver results in a fast-paced team environment
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Flexibility regarding work location (for your development you may need to change work location during the programme)

Your CV should be no longer than 2 pages and clearly outline the following:

  • Details of ALL your qualifications including titles, institutions, years of commencement and (projected) completion with your results to date
  • Your relevant modules and academic projects
  • All your work experience
  • Any relevant external interests / pursuits
  • A contact telephone number (with voicemail enabled)
  • A valid email address to reach you on
