title: Process Controller
description:
Job Description :

Process Controller

Type: 1 year Fixed-Term Contract

About us

With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.

Bring your talent, curiosity and ambition, and strive for your personal best alongside people who challenge, support and learn from each other. Together, as one outstanding team, we keep learning, improving and raising the bar for our brands, our business and each other.

Join us and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

About the Function

Supply Chain & Manufacturing is where our brands are made, moved and delivered to the world.

With over half of our people working across more than 100 sites, this is a complex, large-scale operation that brings together production, logistics, engineering and supplier partnerships.

It’s fast-paced and hands-on, with teams working together to ensure quality, efficiency and sustainability at every stage. From sourcing ingredients to getting products into customers’ hands, you’ll play a role in delivering the brands people know and love.

Join our Beer Team in St. James

In 1759, Arthur Guinness made the bold decision to sign a 9,000 year lease on a brewery site at St. James’s Gate in Dublin, heralding the arrival of what would become one of Ireland’s most iconic brands and best loved beers, GUINNESS® Beer is the primary liquid supply chain of the ISC brewing Business, producing all of Diageo’s outstanding collection of brands like Guinness, Hop House 13, Rockshore and Smithwicks. Beer & Brewing has a constant focus on the marriage of craft & productivity through manufacturing excellence techniques - standardisation and simplification in everything we do. Our success is thanks to the strength of our people, in every role. It’s why we trust them with our legacy. And it’s why we reward them with the career-defining opportunities that they deserve.

About the role

Our Beer operations are made up of approximately 400 employees who are engaged in roles across four locations (St James's Gate, LittleConnell, Belfast Packaging and Runcorn Packaging). As a Process Controller, you'll:

Manufacture products of the highest quality to agreed customer service levels, safely and efficiently.
Operate 2 keg lines and related Process Plant which produces almost 7 million kegs annually consisting of 25 different beer types, 4 different keg sizes and 50 different SKU’s.
Drive the Process Continuous Improvement agenda in the Keg Plant.

Your key responsibilities and accountabilities will be as follows:

At all times adhere to Diageo health and safety, environmental, and food safety standards.
Understand the functions and workings of machines and perform autonomous maintenance tasks.
Manage and control all processes including operation of packaging machinery.
Carry out quality analyses relevant to the role, and ensure quality is right the first time and all data input.
Apply Manufacturing Excellence tools and techniques.

Work Pattern

In this role you'll primarily be on day shift (Mon-Fri) however some shift cover, and flexibility will be required at times.

About you

We’re looking for people with character: driven, resilient, and open-minded. You’ll be commercially astute, target-driven driven, and flexible – as our work can change quickly.

When it comes to experience, you'll be able to demonstrate the following:

Demonstrated detailed understanding of Brewing/Packaging processes, Quality & Environmental systems and Engineering/Maintenance.
Understand how to apply diagnostic and problem-solving skills in a production environment.
Experience of applying continuous improvement techniques in a manufacturing environment.
Experience of working in a high-performance team and delivering agreed objectives.
Understand and be proficient in information systems, e.g. SAP, Harford, Microsoft Office & MES etc.
Knowledge of risk standards (Quality H&S Environment) Safety and hygiene compliance procedures.
Demonstrate a detailed understanding of the Permit to Work system and H&S statutory requirements/ responsibilities/ obligations to the appropriate level.

Working with Us

Flexibility is key to our success. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you so that you’re supported to manage your wellbeing and balance your priorities from day one.

We recognise and value performance, offering our people a highly competitive Rewards and Benefits package.

Our purpose is crafting iconic drinks chosen for life’s moments. And it’s our people, with their different experiences, perspectives and talents, who make that possible.

We value diversity in its broadest sense and want everyone to feel they can belong, contribute and strive for their personal best. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives — challenging, supporting and learning from one another as one outstanding team.

Together, we’re constantly learning and improving, combining the strength of our people, capabilities and iconic brands to raise the bar, grow and win. Wherever you join us, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, make an impact and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

Ready to bring your best? This could be your opportunity.

If you require a reasonable adjustment, please ensure that you capture this information when you submit your application.

Recruitment Scam Warning

Protecting candidates is very important to us. All communications regarding your application will come from an email address ending in @diageo.com. In our recruitment process, we'll never ask for money.

title: Person in Charge
description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and passionate Person in Charge in Tipperary to lead and oversee the delivery of high-quality residential disability services within a designated region. Our client is a specialist provider of residential and community-based services for young people with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Through evidence-based approaches, including Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA), Positive Behaviour Support (PBS), and Equine Therapy, they deliver high-quality, person-centred care in a safe and therapeutic environment, with young people and their families at the centre of all decision-making and support planning.

We are looking for a structured, curious and collaborative Process Specialist with a focus on Trade Compliance. This is a key role for someone who enjoys working across functions, connecting business needs with process design, data, systems and practical ways of working.

Trade Compliance is becoming increasingly important in a complex and changing global regulatory environment. In this role, you will help shape scalable and sustainable processes that support compliant and efficient international business operations.

Job purpose

As Process Specialist – Trade Compliance, you will play a key role in driving the development, alignment and continuous improvement of Trade Compliance processes. You will help translate business and compliance needs into clear process requirements, support digital solutions and enable adoption across an international organisation.

The role requires strong process understanding, stakeholder engagement and the ability to work across business, system and data topics.

You will support process areas such as:

Import and export compliance
Sanctions and denied party screening
Customs documentation and customs procedures
Product classification, country of origin and trade preference processes
Trade Compliance reporting, analytics and data quality
SAP S/4HANA and SAP GTS enabled process solutions

Main responsibilities

Contribute to the alignment and development of Trade Compliance processes across the Mining organisation, ensuring that common ways of working are clear, practical and fit for purpose.
Engage with Trade Compliance stakeholders, process owners, Business Areas and divisions to understand business needs, process pain points, regulatory requirements and improvement opportunities.
Translate business and compliance needs into clear process requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria and documentation to support solution design and delivery.
Take an active role in SAP S/4HANA and SAP GTS related process design, testing, implementation and post go-live support from a Trade Compliance process perspective.
Support and continuously improve process documentation, including future process models, work instructions, training material and other artefacts required for sustainable process ownership.
Support data quality, reporting and analytics initiatives by helping define business requirements, validate outputs and promote self-service reports for Trade Compliance users.
Participate in SAP GTS and other relevant system implementations by supporting testing activities, including preparation of test scenarios, execution of process tests, defect follow-up and user acceptance testing.
Contribute to change impact assessments and contribute to adoption activities, helping business users understand process changes and how they affect daily operations.
Monitor process performance, collect feedback and support continuous improvement activities in close collaboration with the wider process organisation.
Act as a knowledgeable point of contact for Trade Compliance process questions, supporting issue clarification and helping distinguish between process, training, data and system-related topics.
Other Ad hoc duties as requested by management

Experience

You are analytical, structured and comfortable working with complexity. You enjoy asking the right questions, connecting different perspectives and turning business needs into clear and practical process solutions.

You have experience in process work, business analysis, continuous improvement, projects or change initiatives. Experience in Trade Compliance, logistics, customs, SAP S/4HANA, SAP GTS is an advantage, but curiosity, collaboration and a strong process mindset are equally important.

title: Project Design Elec. Engineer, DCC Communities
description:
DESCRIPTION

As a Design Electrical Engineer, you will lead design projects in operational data centers, that remediate issues, upgrade our existing infrastructure and add new services.

Key job responsibilities
You will use your Electrical expertise to:
- Perform design and equipment submittal review for Data Centers in your region.
- Interface with internal and external data center design engineering team, server hardware team, environmental health and safety team, field engineering, and controls engineering to promote standards that maintain consistency and reliability in services delivered.
- Work on concurrent projects, sometimes in multiple geographical regions and act as a technical subject matter expert for your given discipline.
- Support construction, commissioning, operations, and turnover. Are detail and data oriented with familiarity with design/construction processes
- Have experience managing engineering projects and engineering consultants. Build trust and relationships with different stakeholders (e.g., Operations, Commissioning, Construction and Design)

A day in the life
Each day you will interact with different teams responsible for various aspects of the data centers. You will mentor and oversee the work of junior engineers in your discipline. You will have the opportunity to work on projects locally and globally, with up to 25% travel.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel
- Experience in industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Professional Engineer License
- Experience with building codes and regulations for your region
- Experience carrying design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. title: Analyst
description:
We are currently seeking analysts with a minimum of 1 year’s relevant experience working within an energy, safety, water, process industry or a related sector.

‌

The Position

Job Title : Analyst

Starting Salary : *€44,678 (Salary scale: €44,678 - €63,230) *Please see below for further information.

Location : The Exchange, Belgard Square North, Tallaght, Dublin 24.

Working Hours : 37.5 hours per week

Hybrid working : Up to 3 days per week remote working available

Closing Date : 12.00 noon, Monday, 19th October, 2026.

Tenure : Appointment will be on a permanent basis, subject to successful passing of the probationary period.

‌

The Role of Analyst

We are seeking candidates with experience in economics, engineering, legal, public policy and other relevant fields to fill posts in the following areas:

Security of Supply and Wholesale

Ensuring a secure energy transition to 2030, delivering on our 80% renewable electricity target and overseeing the wholesale all-island Single Electricity Market (SEM) in co-operation with the Utility Regulator in Belfast.

Networks and Economic Regulation

Working with Uisce Éireann and energy companies, enhancing the CRU’s economic regulation of these critical networks, ensuring that they support customers, underpin economic growth and play a transformational role in climate change adaptation and mitigation.

Customer Policy and Protection (incl. Legal)

Empowering and protecting customers, overseeing competition and consumer protection across Ireland’s energy retail markets and playing an important role in supporting the National Energy Affordability Taskforce. The Legal, Compliance and Enforcement teams are also part of this Division, providing legal advice and support and compliance and enforcement duties across the organisation on a broad range of regulatory and corporate matters.

Energy Safety

Regulating safety of gas (networks, supply, storage, use and liquefied petroleum gas distribution), petroleum (upstream onshore and offshore exploration and production of hydrocarbons), gas installers and electrical contractors.

Decarbonisation

Delivering new CRU regulatory frameworks for offshore renewables, green hydrogen, district heating and other new technologies and leading cross-cutting decarbonisation projects, including electricity connection policy, interconnector regulation and Projects of Common Interest.

Operations and Organisational Development

Supporting and empowering the CRU teams to achieve outcomes in our Strategic Plan in the areas of process improvement, finance and governance, human resources, information technology, and communications.

‌

Duties and Responsibilities

Reporting to a manager, the successful candidate will be involved in a varied role working to tight deadlines in a dynamic environment. CRU Analyst roles typically include activities such as:

Preparing CRU consultation and decision papers, preparing reports and making presentations both internally and externally.
Working as a member of a team and on specific cross-functional project teams as required.
Engaging with internal and external stakeholders in a constructive manner in order to further CRU objectives.
Engaging with NI, GB or EU counterparts on all-island or EU policy, markets or industry developments.
Maintaining an awareness of policy developments and best practice within the energy and water industry and related industries, both in Ireland and internationally.
Researching policy issues and identifying data/trends, using this to suggest policy courses of action for the CRU.
Analysing spreadsheets of energy/water/safety data, and financial modelling.
Carrying out such other functions as may be required from time to time to fulfil the business objectives of the CRU and as appropriate to the grade.

The above list is not exhaustive. While the successful candidate will be assigned to a particular team within the CRU, they will also be expected to contribute to the work of the wider Division/CRU as requirements dictate.

The CRU may establish a shortlist of suitable candidates for potential future positions that may arise within the organisation.

‌

Qualifications and Experience

Essential Requirements

Candidates must have on or before the closing date for applications the following:

1. An appropriate NFQ Level 8 or higher qualification, preferably in economics, law, engineering, science, health and safety (process safety), business or other closely related discipline;

2. A minimum of 1 year’s relevant experience working within an energy, safety, water, process industry or a related sector.

Desirable Requirements

1. Knowledge/experience of existing and developing policy frameworks in the regulated energy sectors;

2. Experience working in a regulated sector or governmental organisation.

‌

The Package

Salary

*Starting salary of €44,678 (Salary scale: €44,678 - €63,230)

*Candidates should note that entry will be at the minimum point of the scale.
The rate of remuneration may be adjusted in line with the Government pay policy.
Candidates should note that different pay and conditions may apply if, immediately prior to appointment, the appointee is a serving civil or public servant.
Salary increments will be awarded annually, subject to satisfactory performance.

Benefits

Attractive Pension Scheme.
Opportunity to work remotely up to 3 days per week, in addition to up to 6 weeks fully remote.
Access to the cycle-to-work scheme.
Opportunity for further education
25 days of annual leave upon appointment, rising to 29 days after 5 years’ service and 31 days after 10 years’ service.
11 bank holidays/public holidays.
Flexible working arrangements.
Tax saver Bus / Luas scheme available to assist with travel costs to and from work.
Access to CRU’s Employee Assistance Programme.

The CRU will provide you with ongoing support and training, and there will be ample opportunity for professional development, allowing you to maximise your potential and progress you

title: Laboratory Analyst
description:
Company Description

We are SGS – the world’s leading testing, inspection and certification company. We are recognized as the global benchmark for sustainability, quality and integrity. Our 97,000 employees operate a network of 2,650 offices and laboratories, working together to enable a better, safer and more interconnected world.

Job Description

ROLE OVERVIEW

Job Title: Laboratory Analyst
Job Type: Permanent
Location: Unit 1C N11 South Point Business Park, Charvey Lane,, Rathnew, Ireland
Hours: 39 hours p/w
Salary: €35000-52000 pa

Main Purpose of Role

The primary function of this role is to work in the Gas Chromatography laboratory in Rathnew. This includes testing of gas samples using SGS GAS and Pharmacopeia procedures, develop SGS GAS procedures for new & existing GC testing methods and compile reports for the testing.

In this role you will work to cGMP standards and complete work under GAS ISO17025 accreditation.

You will also complete validation testing for new equipment and methods being brought into service under direction and support from the laboratory manager or technical manager. You will develop a knowledge and competence of Gas Chromatography using TCD, FID, PDHID, DID, SCD, MS, and other detection technologies and must have the willingness to learn. Full training will be provided from our offices in Ireland and by external vendors when necessary.

You will work with a team of passionate hands-on engineers, scientists, and other departments of SGS GAS such as the quality team and the field-testing team. You will also work with the wider SGS group.

Good communication skills are required. You must be self-motivated with a “can-do” attitude and be customer focused.

Primary Responsibilities

Work independently and provide guidance and role modelling for Junior staff.
Focus on customer requirements and prioritise workload in the GC lab.
Run the operation meeting for gas testing and instrumentation reports.
Role model clean as you go policy in the GC laboratory and act of the area owner.
Perform a variety of routine sample testing to quantitatively measure gas quality in a variety of products and for different applications.
Execute validated analytical methods with minimal supervision.
Analyse, compile and format results of testing into clear reports for lab and field-testing work in a timely manner.
Prepare GCs for testing and complete system suitability testing.
Assist in development and validation of new basic and complex analysis for GC-TCD/FID/MS/SCD/DID/ECD under supervision.
Problem-solve basic and complex GC technical issues and utilise internal and external expertise to identify and address problems with the minimum impact.
Report issues to the quality department and take part in the relevant investigations.
Comply with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Laboratory Practices (GLP), ISO17025 requirements and all internal processes.
Participate in internal and external laboratory audits under the direction of the SGS-GAS quality manager.
Be willing and able to work as a team member to ensure continuous improvement relative to laboratory functions.
Adhere to all safety protocols.
Be available for occasional weekend work (short shifts – 2 to 4 hours).
On rare occasions travel to customer sites to complete testing and/or technical meetings and reviews.
Complete project work within the SGS laboratory network and SGS customers – potentially on another site for a defined duration.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in science. With 2 years minimum experience in analytical chemistry & Gas Chromatography techniques.

Additional Information

The ideal candidate should possess the following attributes/skillsets

Lead by example in promoting a Health & Safety culture.
Strong attention to detail.
Analytical decision maker.
Be dependable and reliable and able to work in a process driven environment.
To be organised, self-motivated and able to prioritise and manage conflicting needs of the business.
High level of computer literacy.
You should be a strong communicator and have the ability to negotiate both internally and externally with, contractors, customers and colleagues.

Job Description

Deal Onboarding Analyst - Global Corporate Trust

The Deal Onboarding Management (DOM) team sits within the Data Management & Control Group and are responsible for a variety of tasks including but not exclusive to the setup of deals across a variety of systems and platforms, providing client access to statements, deal audit follow up’s and raising of quarterly fees for multiple products. This team works closely with internal/external teams gathering information to support the deal setup. The team sets up deals as per the target operating model and is responsible for flagging issues. title: QC Sample Management Analyst (QCSM)
description:
QC Sample Management Analyst (QCSM)

Dublin 22, Grange Castle

Job Purpose

Responsibility for carrying out sample management tasks pertaining to GC and external site manufactured products, regulatory reserve, stability, and Board of Health samples.

Job Responsibilities

Routinely receive manufacturing test samples and distribute to the appropriate analytical laboratories.
Oversee and maintain appropriate procedures to ensure chain of custody for QC samples is maintained.
Manage the incoming shipment processes from external sites, verification of sample inventory, processing of samples and distribution to QC test laboratories.
Shipment of Drug Product and associated bulk Drug Substance regulatory samples to BOH sites.
Management of stability sample processes including study enrolment, time-point pulls, sample shipment, and study disposal.
Maintenance of the reserve program, including inspection of reserve and retention samples, documentation of inspection results, and maintenance of reserve/retention equipment.
Reference material inventory management.
Perform review and approval of QCSM standard operating procedures, sampling and analysis plans, and stability protocols to ensure compliance.
Facilitate laboratory investigations and support associated product investigations.
Support the preparation and review of QC APQR and periodic review reports.
Partner closely and proactively engage with customers and key stakeholders to understand and deliver samples within specified turnaround times, participating in cross-functional teams as required.
Represent QCSM at product, technical and robustness team meetings and lead/drive associated deliverables.
Contribute to the completion of complex projects, managing own time to meet agreed targets and developing plans for work activities on own projects within a team.
Participate in new initiatives such as the 5S, Standard Work, Data Integrity and IMEX programs as they arise.
Engage with the business to identify and define scope for continuous improvement, robustness, and Best Practice initiatives assisting with improving the efficiency of local and across-site processes and procedures.
Ensure compliance with cGMP, corporate standards/Pfizer Quality System (PQS), site policies/procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Technical writing assignments such as SOPs, trend reports, risk assessments, laboratory investigations, and change controls.
Assist in the maintenance and development of training programs and perform training of other analysts.

title: Legal Analyst
description:
About Us

At Fenergo, we’re not just building software - we’re transforming how the world’s leading financial institutions fight financial crime. Headquartered in Dublin and trusted by over 100 of the world’s top financial institutions, we’re on a mission to change the game.

We’re more than a global leader in AI-powered client lifecycle management - we’re reimagining how financial institutions tackle compliance. From Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) to rapidly evolving regulations, we turn complexity into clarity. Our FinCrime Operating System, powered by agentic AI and intelligent automation, helps financial institutions move faster, act smarter, and stay safer across 120+ countries.

But we don’t stop there.

At Fenergo, we believe in a world where financial institutions aren’t just compliant - they’re confident. Where technology doesn’t just meet regulations - it stays ahead of them. Our mission is to empower financial institutions to stop financial crime and create a safer world.

Every product we build, every innovation we deliver, and every partnership we forge is shaped by that belief. We’re tackling some of the toughest challenges in financial technology. From speeding up onboarding to uncovering hidden risks, our work empowers banks to serve their customers with speed, integrity, and peace of mind.

Join us, and be part of a team that’s building smart solutions, solving real problems, and shaping the future - together.

Who are you?

You are a high-achieving, recent Law graduate keen to launch a stellar career as a commercial lawyer. But, right now, your plans may be on hold because you are waiting to finish FE-1s or secure a traineeship. You wish there was a place where you could work now to put your degree to use and get real legal and business experience.

Why should you join us?

If that’s who you are, and you are hard-working, diligent, self-motivating and enjoy being part of an organisation with exciting revenue growth plans, we would like to speak to you. Fenergo is shaping the future of our industry, and you will be afforded an opportunity to significantly impact the revenue growth of a major target market for the company.

What you will do?

As a Fenergo Legal Analyst, you will be a member of our Legal Department reporting directly to our Head of Legal (Sales & Commercial). With training and oversight by our experienced team of lawyers, you will facilitate sales of Fenergo’s technology products to our customers. Many of whom are global financial institutions – names you will know! You will help review contracts, prepare for negotiations with our customers’ legal and procurement teams, and assist with advice to Fenergo’s business leaders. You will also have opportunities to learn how our business operates by liaising with Fenergo’s commercial, technical and financial teams.

Responsibilities:

Assist in all aspects of commercial contract review.
Prepare for contract negotiations with customers by drafting responses to customer legal and commercial requests.
Review customer relationship documents and other information to help provide strategic advice to Fenergo business leaders.
Assist generally with the operations of the Fenergo Legal Department.

Requirements

Key Expectations:

High-achieving Law graduate.
Keen interest in commercial law.
Intellectually curious.
Dogged determination to learn.
Superior attention to detail.
Excellent writing skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues to achieve common goals.

Benefits

What’s In It For You?

Healthcare cover
Pension
Employee Assistance Programme
Opportunity to earn an annual company bonus
23 days annual leave
3 company closure days
Extensive training programs, classroom and online, through ‘Fenergo University’
Other competitive company benefits, such as flexible working hours, work from home policy, sports and social committee and much more
Buddy system for all new starters
Opportunity to work on a cutting-edge Fintech Product, using the latest of tools and technologies.
Defined training and role tracking to allow you see and assess your own career development and progress.
Work From Home set-up allowance

Diversity, Equality, and Inclusivity

Fenergo is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, where all employees are valued, respected, and can reach their full potential. We do not discriminate based on race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Our hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We believe that a diverse workforce enriches our company culture, fosters innovation, and contributes to our overall success. We strive to provide a fair and supportive environment for all employees, promoting equal opportunities for career development and advancement. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply for employment opportunities and join our team in contributing to a collaborative and inclusive work environment.

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. Job Description

The Quality Compliance Specialist is responsible for supporting and maintaining the site's Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure compliance with AbbVie standards, cGMP requirements, and applicable regulatory guidelines. The role plays a key part in ensuring that products manufactured at AbbVie consistently meet the expectations of patients, regulatory authorities, and the company.

Coordinate and maintain the site Quality Management System, ensuring compliance with AbbVie policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
Lead and support Product Quality Review (PQR) activities.
Manage technical agreements, including initiation, review, approval, implementation, and document control.
Coordinate quality metrics, track-and-trend activities, and performance reporting to support Manufacturing and Quality Control operations.
Drive the application of Quality Risk Management (QRM) principles across site activities, including Risk Control Strategies (RCS) and FMEA processes.
Support investigations of customer complaints, deviations, and non-conformances, ensuring robust CAPA implementation and effectiveness verification.
Provide quality oversight and approval for validation activities, including systems, processes, and equipment.
Support New Product Introduction (NPI) projects and collaborate closely with Manufacturing, Technical Operations, and Laboratory functions.

Coordinate change control activities and assess quality impact associated with proposed changes.
Provide guidance to site personnel on cGMP, quality system requirements, and regulatory expectations.
Act as a key liaison with corporate quality functions and regulatory agencies, including HPRA, FDA, and other regulatory authorities.
Perform regulatory assessments and policy reviews to ensure ongoing compliance.
Initiate and manage quality event records, investigations, and CAPA activities as required.
Support supplier quality activities, including vendor qualification, supplier performance monitoring, notifications, and audits.
Participate in and support internal audits, regulatory inspections, customer audits, and inspection readiness activities, including audit responses and evidence management.
Contribute to continuous improvement and compliance initiatives across the site.
Ensure adherence to all Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) standards, procedures, and policies.

Qualifications

Required

Third-level qualification in Science, Quality, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Minimum of 2 years' experience in a Quality Assurance, Quality Compliance, or related GMP environment.
Strong knowledge of cGMP requirements and pharmaceutical regulatory expectations.
Experience working within a Quality Management System in a regulated manufacturing environment.

Preferred

Experience supporting regulatory inspections and audits.
Knowledge of quality risk management, change control, CAPA, supplier quality, and validation processes.
Experience within the pharmaceutical, biologics, or medical device industry.

Skills & Competencies

Strong attention to detail with a commitment to quality and compliance.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to assess and interpret regulatory requirements and implement effective solutions.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, both written and verbal.
Proven ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams.
Results-driven mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and Right First Time principles.
High level of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.
Ability to influence stakeholders and drive compliance-focused outcomes.

title: FOC Technical Specialist, Facility Operations Center (FOC)
description:
DESCRIPTION

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth! Amazon is a place where builders can build. We hire the world's brightest minds and offer them an environment in which they can invent and innovate to improve the experience for our customers. If you'd like to help us build a place where you can find and buy anything online, this is the job for you.

The AWS Data Center Community (DCC) organization is looking for an individual with proven and tested leadership skills to join the Facility Operation Center (FOC) team. The FOC launched as a singular support team to proactively monitor the life-safety systems and the infrastructure equipment alarms that provides power and cooling to the platform on a global 24x7x365 basis. We support Data Center Engineer Operations teams who are responsible for the operation of infrastructure equipment.

The FOC Technical Specialist facilitates and deep dives customer impacting events, locates systemic infrastructure issues using data driven analysis to drive solutions and serves as a subject matter expert on department processes. The FOC Technical Specialist is responsible for the design, creation, and launch of new learning content, creating and maintaining all FOC documentation globally, and managing the technical training of the team across the regions. You will play a significant role in the career development of the global FOC team by mentoring and helping managers guide the career growth of their team members. You are responsible for leading team members across regions and functional areas to accomplish organizational goals. You will guide the team on improving operational efficiency for all services through the identification and development of SLAs, metrics, workflows, procedures, tools, and documentation. You will lead data analysis and engagement of stakeholder teams to drive corrective actions by utilizing processes, such as After-Action Reports (AAR), Correction of Errors (COE), AWS Emergency Response protocols, Lessons Learned, and Global Action Items. You will be responsible for delivering global projects while influencing stakeholders by creating reports, improving processes, and presenting narratives. You will be expected to run effective projects and programs independently. You will support team goals and projects by providing feedback and technical support as required.

Key job responsibilities
- Provides support to the team during Critical Site (CSE) and Large Scale (LSE) events. Acts as FOC POC in the COE process.
- Deep dives post event data and reviews all After Action Reports (AAR) to ensure standards are met.
- Meet or exceed FOC KPI’s in project delivery to develop and drive FOC Engineer. efficiency projects which reduce manual tasks.
- Meet or exceed FOC KPI’s in tracking project/program quality of 85%.
- Author and present AWS business continuity and emergency response program documents.
- Ability to lead DC availability meetings and post event analysis to senior leadership.
- Ownership and driving organizational and team level goals
- Continuous integration with stakeholder teams on program improvements.
- Locates systemic infrastructure issues using data driven analysis to drive solutions.
- Collaborates with external teams to implement new processes to reduce waste.
- Creates and maintains FOC technical documentation driving process improvements.
- Manages technical training to ensure engineers meet the bar for engineering knowledge.
- Designs, creates and implements learning content, practical assessments, and facilitates workshops and instructor led training programs.

description:

Location: Dublin

About Us:

Tuath Housing ("Tuath") has provided safe, secure, and affordable housing since 2006. A lot has changed over the years, but our values remain the same. In partnership with key stakeholders, our main focus is on delivering more quality homes to more people and providing an outstanding Customer experience to over 39,000 residents. Working with Tuath is different because we make a difference. We maintain and develop our team of dedicated, motivated, and authentic people through focused training and career development.

Our People and Culture:

Tuath is accredited with the Silver Award from Investors for Diversity and are committed to promoting a diverse and respectful workplace reflective of all cultures, nationalities, backgrounds, genders, members of the LGBTQ+ community and people from traditionally marginalised backgrounds. Tuath is committed to embedding environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations into every aspect of the business, and to implementing a business plan that emphasizes social responsibility throughout our operations. We believe in the importance and value of working in partnership with our stakeholders to deliver more homes to more people, creating communities across the country. As Tuath continues to grow, the role will help ensure that our people practices, management capability and organisational structures develop at the same pace as the organisation. If you are driven to make a difference and believe that everybody needs a home, Tuath is waiting to hear from you.

Position Summary:

To design, deliver and embed practical learning and capability solutions that improve manager effectiveness, onboarding quality, performance enablement, employee development, and organisational capability across Tuath. The role acts as the specialist lead for learning and capability development, translating organisational priorities, employee feedback, performance insights and workforce needs into structured learning programmes, practical tools, and measurable development interventions. The role is intended to build learning infrastructure where capability is currently limited and to support a consistent organisation-wide approach to manager development, onboarding, performance support, graduate development, and career pathways. This role will also support the responsible use of AI-enabled learning tools to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and personalisation of learning content, while ensuring appropriate governance, quality control and data protection standards are maintained.

Key areas of responsibility

Learning programme design and delivery

Design, develop, deliver, and evaluate practical learning programmes aligned to organisational need.

Create structured learning materials, facilitator guides, manager toolkits, and participant resources.

Personally facilitate workshops, training sessions and structured learning interventions for managers and employees.

Ensure learning content is practical, accessible, and capable of being applied in day-to-day manager and employee practice.

Blend face-to-face workshops, digital micro-learning, peer learning, coaching approaches, and practical workplace assignments.

Design and implement Tuath's Management Essentials Programme for people managers.

Develop practical manager training modules covering core people management responsibilities.

Facilitate manager workshops on topics such as probation, performance, feedback, absence, engagement, communication, and team development.

Support leadership development activity linked to organisational priorities and manager capability gaps.

Provide practical tools and resources that improve manager confidence, consistency, and accountability.

Digital Learning and Innovation

Use appropriate digital tools to support learning needs analysis, content development, learning pathways, manager resources and evaluation.

Develop practical and accessible digital and micro-learning resources that can be used across a multi-site organisation.

Ensure all learning materials are accurate, inclusive, relevant and aligned with Tuath's policies and values.

Identify opportunities to improve the accessibility, consistency and reach of learning through digital approaches.

Use AI-enabled tools selectively and responsibly where they provide a clear benefit, with appropriate quality control, confidentiality and data protection safeguards.

Onboarding, probation, and core learning journeys

Design and own the organisation-wide onboarding and probation learning framework. Develop structured new-starter, new-manager, and probation support materials.

Create role-based learning journeys for employees moving into new or expanded responsibilities.

Ensure onboarding and probation learning supports consistency, clarity, and early performance expectations.

Support performance enablement through learning interventions linked to the performance cycle.

Use performance cycle insight, employee feedback, and manager feedback to identify development priorities.

Support the development of career pathways and internal mobility initiatives.

Create practical resources to support employee development, career conversations, and progression planning.

Graduate programme and emerging talent

Design and implement a structured Graduate Programme.

Develop a graduate learning pathway, rotation support model, and programme calendar.

Support graduate development, manager guidance, progress tracking, and programme evaluation.

Link graduate development to succession planning and future workforce needs.

Learning data, evaluation, and reporting

Use employee survey results, learning feedback, performance cycle data, and HR reporting to identify learning needs.

title: IT/OT Systems & Integration Engineer - Operations Systems Support
description:
Vacancy Number: 29249
Category: Engineering - Other
Job Type: Full-time

Position Description

The Operations Systems Support (OSS) team within ESB Networks' Distribution Markets and System Operations (DMSO) function are seeking to fill the role of Senior IT/Operational Technology (OT) Systems and Integration Engineer. The role of the OSS team is to support and maintain ESB Networks mission critical OT systems enable the monitoring, control, and management of Ireland's electricity distribution network. These include Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), Electricity Distribution Network Management System (NMS) and Geographic Information System (GIS). These systems support real-time network operations, outage management, fault response, service restoration, and data exchange across multiple business and operational platforms.

This role provides a unique opportunity to support capabilities that form part of Ireland's critical national infrastructure. You will work at the forefront of Operational Technology, supporting the processes that underpin transformation of the electricity network as ESB Networks delivers the systems required for increased renewable generation, network flexibility, electrification and the transition to a net-zero future

The Senior IT/OT Systems and Integration Engineer is responsible for supporting, maintaining and enhancing ESB Networks’ critical Operational Technology systems, including NMS, SCADA and associated applications. The role ensures these business-critical platforms remain secure, resilient and available to support network operations, outage management and service restoration. Working closely with business and technology stakeholders, you will help deliver the technologies that support the ongoing transformation of Ireland’s electricity network.

The position involves delivering enhancements to the existing OT systems, supporting system upgrades and patch deployments, troubleshooting complex technical issues, and carrying out data management activities such as housekeeping, environment refreshes, and data integrity maintenance. The Senior IT/OT Systems & Integration Engineer is also responsible for developing and maintaining custom interfaces and integrations between OT systems and ESB or third-party applications ensuring seamless data exchange and operational effectiveness across the organisation.

A key element of the role is working with OT vendors, providing oversight across system support and enhancement activities. Responsibilities include reviewing and approving change requests, supporting the implementation of new functionality, coordinating problem resolution, and engaging with vendor support teams at all levels to ensure timely and effective issue management.

In addition to technical responsibilities, the role has a strong focus on knowledge management and capability development. This includes producing and maintaining high-quality technical documentation, standard operating procedures, configuration records, user guides, and operational runbooks to support effective system operation and support. The Senior IT/OT Systems & Integration Engineer will also play an important role in mentoring and developing junior team members, promoting knowledge transfer, supporting structured training programmes, and building sustainable technical capability within the Technical Operations team.

Key Responsibilities:

Support and maintain ESB Networks critical OT systems, including Electricity Distribution
NMS and SCADA, ensuring the system availability, reliability, and performance.
Troubleshoot and resolve complex application, integration, and operational technology issues within the OT systems.
Support, maintain, and develop custom interfaces between the OT systems and ESB and third-party systems, ensuring the effective integration and exchange of operational data.
Support, maintain, and enhance custom Electricity Distribution NMS reporting functionality to meet operational and business reporting requirements.
Perform data maintenance activities, including data maintenance and data quality activities, validation, and data refreshes across OT environments.
Support the development and optimisation of advanced Distribution Management System (DMS) capabilities including, Power Flow Analysis, Fault Location, Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), Load Forecasting, Network Optimisation.
Contribute to the ongoing evolution of smart network capabilities that support increased renewable generation, electrification and network flexibility.
Delivery of enhancement projects for the existing OT systems, ensuring alignment with operational and strategic objectives.
Work with OT system vendors to ensure issue resolution, review and approve change requests, guide the implementation of new functionality, and coordinate effectively with vendor support teams to ensure systems remain stable, secure, and aligned with operational and business requirements
Support the delivery of new projects including system upgrades and problem resolution activities.
Support testing activities, including system, integration, user acceptance, and regression testing for upgrades, enhancements, and new functionality.
Work closely with the wider OSS team, OT Delivery, Enterprise IT Services, the OT vendors, and business stakeholders to ensure the successful operation and continuous improvement of critical real-time operational systems.
Work closely with other areas of the business to understand operational requirements, address system issues, and deliver effective technology solutions.

title: Software Engineer in Test
Test Automation Engineer
description:
Test Automation Engineer

Location – Remote anywhere from Republic of Ireland

Contract type - Permanent Fulltime

Work model – Remote

Working hours - (Monday to Thursday 8:30am -5:30pm and Friday 8:30am -3:15pm)


* We can only consider applicants eligible to work full-time in the Republic of Ireland.

Candidates must be based in the Republic of Ireland


Our client is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation


You will be working within and promoting the Company Values – Be Brave, Be Wise, Be Proud and Exceed.


Role Overview

You will design, build and own the automated testing capability underpinning releases for a B2B SaaS platform serving enterprise clients.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will be responsible for replacing manual test execution with reliable, maintainable automation integrated into CI/CD pipelines, and for raising the overall quality engineering standard of the team.


Key Responsibilities

Automation design and development

  • Design, build and maintain automated test frameworks covering functional, regression, API and end-to-end scenarios.
  • Develop and maintain automated test suites for web applications, REST APIs and platform integrations.
  • Identify existing manual test cases suitable for automation, prioritise them by risk and effort, and systematically convert them.
  • Build and manage the test data, environments and fixtures needed to run suites reliably and repeatably.

CI/CD and quality engineering

  • Integrate automated test execution into CI/CD pipelines so that quality feedback is delivered on every build.
  • Define and maintain quality gates, coverage targets and release criteria alongside engineering leads.
  • Monitor suite health, investigate and eliminate flaky tests, and keep execution times within acceptable limits.
  • Report on quality metrics — coverage, pass rates, defect escape rates — and use them to drive improvement.

Quality assurance and collaboration

  • Work with developers, DevOps and product stakeholders to define acceptance criteria and testable requirements from the outset.
  • Perform exploratory and risk-based testing where automation is not appropriate, and carry out root-cause analysis on escaped defects.
  • Support non-functional testing, including performance, load and security-related validation.
  • Mentor colleagues in automation practice and promote quality ownership across the wider team.
  • Evaluate and adopt new tooling, including AI-assisted testing approaches, where it demonstrably improves coverage or reduces effort.

Education

  • A technology, engineering or computer science related bachelor’s degree, or equivalent demonstrable experience.

Mandatory Candidate Requirements

  • 4+ years’ experience in test automation within a commercial software or B2B SaaS environment.
  • Strong programming ability in at least one of Python, Java, C# or JavaScript/TypeScript, with the capability to build and maintain a framework rather than only write scripts.
  • Hands-on experience with modern UI automation tooling such as Playwright, Selenium or Cypress.
  • Demonstrable experience automating API and integration testing (for example REST Assured, Postman/Newman, pytest or equivalent).
  • Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines, ideally Azure DevOps, and working with source control and branching workflows.
  • Solid grounding in test design: risk-based prioritisation, coverage analysis, and knowing what should and should not be automated.
  • Experience working in an Agile development environment.
  • Native proficiency in spoken and written English, with the ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Desirable but not Mandatory

  • Performance and load testing experience (JMeter, k6, Locust or similar).
  • Working knowledge of Azure cloud services, containerisation and infrastructure-as-code.
  • SQL and database testing experience.
  • Experience with AI-assisted test generation, maintenance or triage tooling.
  • Security testing awareness (for example OWASP fundamentals).
  • ISTQB or equivalent certification.

What about you?

This is the most important part. The role suits an engineer who takes genuine ownership of quality, is curious about why defects occur rather than just that they did, and who wants to build something durable rather than patch what exists.

You will be joining a collaborative and highly regarded team where engineering standards are taken seriously, so we are looking for people who understand what it takes to sustain that.




Why Join Us

title: Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals
description:
Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals

About Tyndall
Tyndall National Institute is an international leader in semiconductors, photonics and deep-tech research and innovation. As a leading collaborative European research institute, Tyndall is a key actor and hosting partner in the delivery of the ‘Chips for Europe Initiative’ (EU Chips Act).

Tyndall is Ireland’s leading research and innovation organisation and it is the national focal point for excellence in deep-tech research, development and graduate training at the convergence of nanotechnology, microelectronics, photonics, electronics and AI. Tyndall is recognised as an international research leader in semiconductor, chip and digital technologies, particularly as applied to the fields of Information & Communications, Health & Life Sciences, Agritech & Food Security, Energy and Climate Mitigation, emerging fields such as quantum, and novel computing paradigms.

The Institute’s key objective is to see frontier research activities having a significant impact on economic development and societal challenges in Ireland, Europe and beyond. Central to Tyndall’s mission is delivering economic impact through research excellence in partnership with industry and academia. With an annual turnover of more than €50m, the Institute has a community of over 600 researchers, engineers, support staff, postgraduate students, interns and industry researchers-in-residence.

With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland.

Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation.

About the Team
The integrated circuits group at Tyndall National Institute consist of a large team of researchers in silicon chip design, at various stages of their careers; from Masters researcher through to Principal Researcher. All are creating advanced, innovative and high impact Integrated Circuit technologies, which will shape our future lives. Excellent research is being carried out in areas such as Analog Precision Circuits, RF and Millimeter-wave Communications circuits, Cryogenic CMOS and Integrated Power Systems.

About the Role
Design of a Wide-bandwidth (RF) low noise amplifier
The objective of this position is to apply AI assisted circuit design methods to design amplifiers and Analog to Digital converter blocks. The circuit blocks will be used to build a system to capture Bio electrical signals like ECG and EMG.

Key Duties & Responsibilities
The candidate is expected to be creative, self-motivated, and should help create an efficientl and friendly atmosphere within the Integrated Circuits Group and beyond to all teams at Tyndall.
Propose AI assisted design methods to Simulate, Design and Layout analogue circuits either using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from industry standard vendors like Cadence or custom or open source tools.
With guidance from the senior Tyndall design team propose innovative circuits to meet the bio sensing application
Perform schematic design, simulation and analysis across PVT corners and relevant operating conditions.
Work with guidance from experienced layout engineers to ensure effective layout implementation of analogue circuits, including matching, parasitics, shielding, grounding, isolation and other layout considerations
Prepare presentations and reports.
Support project management.
Participate in Education and Public Engagement activities, as required.
Ensure compliance with Tyndall’s Quality Management Systems, Health and Safety standards, and other regulations.
Carry out any additional duties as may reasonably be required within the general scope and level of the post.
Essential Criteria

The successful candidate must have:
a MEng or equivalent experience (e.g. BEng + 2 years’ experience) in a relevant discipline such as electrical/electronic engineering, physics or related relevant discipline;
experience in designing integrated circuits in the areas of Analogue, Mixed-Signal or RF circuit design;
experience with designing and simulating integrated circuits using tools such as Cadence/Siemens-Mentor/Synoposys;
strong communication skills, as evidenced by prior experience such as working with/in industry, scientific paper writing, conference presentation and report writing.
Knowledge of analogue circuits e.g. amplifiers or comparators.
Knowledge of AI algorithms
Desirable Criteria
Knowledge of Integrated circuit layout
Good mathematical ability and knowledge of statistics.
Experience programming with Python
What We Offer

Apart from offering a position in a highly successful and positive research environment, with a collaborative ethos full of diverse competencies to boost your career, we offer the following:

Impactful Work: Opportunities to contribute to ground-breaking research and innovation that shape Ireland’s economy and the society at large.
Continuous Learning: Strong support for formal training, further study and professional development.
Interdisciplinary Environment: Where academia, industry, and innovation intersect - supported by cutting-edge infrastructure and expert knowledge.
Blended Working: Flexibility to work remotely and on-site, where the role allows.
Comprehensive Benefits: Access to UCC pension, long-term illness benefit, life assurance, and more.
Generous Leave: Competitive annual leave entitlements.
Equity & Inclusion: Athena Swan Bronze award holder, with ongoing initiatives

AWS has successfully launched the European Sovereign Cloud (ESC), marking a significant development in Utility Computing (UC). title: Software Engineering - Internship 2027
description:
Build the tool our engineers use to run a quantum computing platform

Horizon Quantum's platform compiles and executes quantum programs on real quantum processors around the world. Every day, jobs flow through it: submitted, compiled, queued, run, returned. When one of those jobs fails, our engineers currently piece the story together from several systems at once.

You'll build the tool that fixes that. Over the course of the internship, a small team of interns will design and ship an internal operations platform that gives our Engineering and Support teams a single place to monitor the system, investigate failures, and act on live jobs. It will be used by the people sitting next to you, and it may still be in use after you go back to college.

About Horizon Quantum and Triple Alpha

Horizon Quantum is building software infrastructure that empowers developers to use quantum computing to solve the world’s toughest computational problems. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons, a leading researcher, UCD alumnus and former professor with more than two decades of experience in quantum computing, the company is bridging the gap between today’s quantum hardware and tomorrow’s applications through the creation of advanced software development tools. Its integrated development environment, Triple Alpha, enables developers to write sophisticated, hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction.

Built with proprietary Turing-complete languages and an optimizing compiler, Triple Alpha empowers developers to build complex hardware-agnostic quantum programs. In Triple Alpha, users can work at multiple levels of abstraction—from higher-level algorithm design to hardware-specific control.

Beyond higher-level programming tools, Triple Alpha gives developers access to advanced capabilities supported by Horizon’s underlying execution infrastructure. Users can code, compile, and optimize programs seamlessly across a range of processors and simulators, with built-in resource analysis and single-step API deployment.

What you'll build

A web application, backed by real services and real data, with the following at its core:

A searchable, filterable view of every job the platform has processed and the ability to drill into any one of them for the full picture.
Operational control and job management.
Integration between jobs and engineering tickets.
Live visibility into platform health and usage through dashboards and alerts.
How the internship runs

You'll work as a team, with our teams, and with a real degree of design authority and mentorship from our full time engineers throughout.

Requirements and investigation. Understand the existing system and its data model. Decide what's in scope and what isn't. Identify the constraints you're working within.
System design. Produce the architecture, including components and services, data flows, API specification, data access design, security and authorisation model, error handling, logging and monitoring, deployment, testing strategy. You'll present and defend this before writing production standard code.
Implementation. Build it, using the practices we use: Git, code review, issue tracking, automated testing, coding standards, separated environments, secure credential handling.
Testing. Unit, API, integration, frontend and end-to-end tests, covering the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones.
Documentation and handover. Architecture, local setup, deployment, configuration, API reference, troubleshooting, known limitations, and where you'd take it next.

You'll present your progress and findings to the wider Horizon Quantum team as you go.

What you'll come away with
A production system in use by professional engineers, and the story of how you designed it.
Full-stack experience, including frontend, services, APIs, data, integrations, observability, and deployment.
Practice at the parts of engineering that courses rarely teach, such as scoping ambiguous requirements, defending an architecture, writing documentation someone else needs, and building something secure enough to point at production.
A working understanding of how a commercial quantum computing platform actually operates.
Colleagues and a network in one of the most interesting corners of today’s technology industry.
Who we're looking for

You don't need a quantum computing background. You need to be a capable software engineer who wants to be challenged.

We're looking for:

Students in the final year of a computer science, software engineering or related degree, or on a master's programme
Solid programming ability in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript, or a comparable language
Familiarity with web application development and relational databases
The instinct to ask what a system is really for before building it
Clear communication, including in writing
Self-direction, and the follow-through to finish what you start

Useful, not essential:

React, FastAPI or PostgreSQL specifically
Experience with REST API design, testing frameworks, Docker or CI/CD
Any prior exposure to production systems, monitoring or on-call work
Curiosity about quantum computing (the interest matters more than the knowledge)
Practicalities
Location: Our offices, Dublin 2, Ireland. This is an on-site internship.
Duration: 7 months, February to August 2027.
Paid: Yes. €2100 per month.

About the Team

The Agent Measurement & Forecasting (AMF) team builds Workday's single source of truth for how the company measures and forecasts AI agent performance. We own the data pipeline, metric governance, and semantic layer that turn raw agent telemetry into consistent, auditable metrics used across Agents. Our stack runs on dbt, Apache Iceberg, and MetricsFlow, backed by CI/CD schema enforcement, so every metric we publish carries the same rigor as production code. As Workday scales via a broader agentic transformation, the metrics AMF governs are what let the company trust, and act on, how its agents are performing.

As a Software Engineer, you will work towards technical design and execution for core components of AMF's metrics platform. You'll build and operate the pipeline that lands agent telemetry into Iceberg via dbt, enforce schema contracts through CI/CD gates, and extend the MetricsFlow semantic layer that serves governed metrics to the Product Data Store and downstream consumers. This is a hands-on role: you'll work on multi-tenant data isolation, low-latency query performance for metric serving, and the migration path from today's per-tier governance model. You will drive engineering excellence within the team and act as a domain expert for pipeline design, schema governance, and semantic-layer serving.

Experience with large-scale data processing frameworks such as Spark, Flink, or Kafka within complex distributed architectures
Practical experience with API development (gRPC, REST) for serving metrics and data products to downstream consumers
Understanding of multi-tenant data isolation and security principles, including data encryption and tenant-scoped authorization, relevant to governing tenanted (Tier 0) vs. non-tenanted (Tier 1) data
Strong grasp of distributed systems principles: data partitioning, eventual consistency, and fault tolerance
Solid understanding of Object-Oriented Design (OOD) principles and architectural patterns for scalable, maintainable data systems
Experience with source control management (Git, GitHub/Bitbucket) and collaborative distributed development workflows

title: Software Engineering - Internship 2027
description:
Build the tool our engineers use to run a quantum computing platform

Horizon Quantum's platform compiles and executes quantum programs on real quantum processors around the world. Every day, jobs flow through it: submitted, compiled, queued, run, returned. When one of those jobs fails, our engineers currently piece the story together from several systems at once.

You'll build the tool that fixes that. Over the course of the internship, a small team of interns will design and ship an internal operations platform that gives our Engineering and Support teams a single place to monitor the system, investigate failures, and act on live jobs. It will be used by the people sitting next to you, and it may still be in use after you go back to college.

About Horizon Quantum and Triple Alpha

Horizon Quantum is building software infrastructure that empowers developers to use quantum computing to solve the world’s toughest computational problems. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons, a leading researcher, UCD alumnus and former professor with more than two decades of experience in quantum computing, the company is bridging the gap between today’s quantum hardware and tomorrow’s applications through the creation of advanced software development tools. Its integrated development environment, Triple Alpha, enables developers to write sophisticated, hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction.

Built with proprietary Turing-complete languages and an optimizing compiler, Triple Alpha empowers developers to build complex hardware-agnostic quantum programs. In Triple Alpha, users can work at multiple levels of abstraction—from higher-level algorithm design to hardware-specific control.

Beyond higher-level programming tools, Triple Alpha gives developers access to advanced capabilities supported by Horizon’s underlying execution infrastructure. Users can code, compile, and optimize programs seamlessly across a range of processors and simulators, with built-in resource analysis and single-step API deployment.


What you'll build

A web application, backed by real services and real data, with the following at its core:

  • A searchable, filterable view of every job the platform has processed and the ability to drill into any one of them for the full picture.
  • Operational control and job management.
  • Integration between jobs and engineering tickets.
  • Live visibility into platform health and usage through dashboards and alerts.

How the internship runs

You'll work as a team, with our teams, and with a real degree of design authority and mentorship from our full time engineers throughout.

  • Requirements and investigation. Understand the existing system and its data model. Decide what's in scope and what isn't. Identify the constraints you're working within.
  • System design. Produce the architecture, including components and services, data flows, API specification, data access design, security and authorisation model, error handling, logging and monitoring, deployment, testing strategy. You'll present and defend this before writing production standard code.
  • Implementation. Build it, using the practices we use: Git, code review, issue tracking, automated testing, coding standards, separated environments, secure credential handling.
  • Testing. Unit, API, integration, frontend and end-to-end tests, covering the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones.
  • Documentation and handover. Architecture, local setup, deployment, configuration, API reference, troubleshooting, known limitations, and where you'd take it next.

You'll present your progress and findings to the wider Horizon Quantum team as you go.

What you'll come away with

  • A production system in use by professional engineers, and the story of how you designed it.
  • Full-stack experience, including frontend, services, APIs, data, integrations, observability, and deployment.
  • Practice at the parts of engineering that courses rarely teach, such as scoping ambiguous requirements, defending an architecture, writing documentation someone else needs, and building something secure enough to point at production.
  • A working understanding of how a commercial quantum computing platform actually operates.
  • Colleagues and a network in one of the most interesting corners of today’s technology industry.

Who we're looking for

You don't need a quantum computing background. You need to be a capable software engineer who wants to be challenged.

We're looking for:

  • Students in the final year of a computer science, software engineering or related degree, or on a master's programme
  • Solid programming ability in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript, or a comparable language
  • Familiarity with web application development and relational databases
  • The instinct to ask what a system is really for before building it
  • Clear communication, including in writing
  • Self-direction, and the follow-through to finish what you start

Useful, not essential:

  • React, FastAPI or PostgreSQL specifically
  • Experience with REST API design, testing frameworks, Docker or CI/CD
  • Any prior exposure to production systems, monitoring or on-call work
  • Curiosity about quantum computing (the interest matters more than the knowledge)

Practicalities

  • Location: Our offices, Dublin 2, Ireland. This is an on-site inte
